2026/2875.title: Security Analysis of Anonymous Authentication in Apple's Private Cloud Compute
2026/2875.abstract: Apple's Private Cloud Compute (PCC) offloads on-device computation, such as large language-model prompts, to the cloud while seeking to preserve the privacy users expect from local processing. At its core lies a custom authentication protocol that must reconcile three competing goals: restricting access to registered users within a rate limit, doing so without revealing user identities or linking their requests, and nonetheless retaining the ability to hold misbehaving users accountable. Apple's protocol combines blind RSA signatures in a hierarchical issuance with a salted-hash binding trick,

2026/2874.title: Triads below the ISA: Optimizing Cryptographic Software in CPU Microcode
2026/2874.abstract: Cryptographic software is typically optimized for the instruction set architecture exposed by the processor. Modern processors, however, contain deeper execution layers with computational capabilities and constraints that differ from those of the instruction set architecture (ISA). This work explores the programmable microcode layer in x86 as an implementation target. We characterize the microcode domain as a distinct target architecture for cryptographic computation and adapt implementations to the state, operations, invocation interface, capacity, and scheduling resources it exposes. 2026/2873.title: Optimized Solving Strategy and Two-Step Estimator for LWE with Hints
2026/2873.abstract: Side-channel hints can reduce the cost of solving the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem. We optimize a two-step strategy for LWE with hints that uses BKZ reduction followed by final lattice sieving. Given a lattice constructed from the hints and a specified pair of reduction and sieving algorithms, the strategy jointly selects BKZ block sizes, tour counts, and a final sieving configuration. We also introduce a two-step estimator that predicts the reduced-basis profile and estimates the probability of secret recovery. 2026/2872.title: On the Security of the Cubic UOV Variant CML
2026/2872.abstract: CML is a cubic multivariate signature scheme proposed over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q = 2^8$. Earlier cubic Oil--Vinegar variants such as CUOV and CSSv were broken by differential and high-rank attacks. CML adds an $\ell$-invertible cycle system and a secret position-hiding map to hide the cubic positions. We show that the cubic homogeneous parts of the public key span a space of dimension at most two, so a publicly derived output combination has degree at most two. 2026/2871.title: The Price of Geometry for Private Distance-Sensitive Filters: $\ell_\infty$ versus $\ell_2$
2026/2871.abstract: A distance-sensitive set representation stores a set $S$ in a metric space and must accept points within distance $r$ of $S$ and reject points farther than $cr$, each with error probability at most $\alpha$. Under differential privacy, even exact membership costs a privacy loss of $\ln(1/\alpha)$; we ask how much \emph{more} the geometry of the space forces. Earlier lower bounds cover only restricted mechanisms, such as partition-based ones or those whose outputs contain no scattered false positives (``dust''). We prove lower bounds for every mechanism. 2026/2870.title: BMRaccoon: Blind Multi-Signatures from Lattices
2026/2870.abstract: Blind multi-signatures (BMS) allow a user to obtain a compact signature on a hidden message through the joint participation of multiple signers, providing a basis for decentralized issuance of anonymous tokens.We present BMRaccoon, the first lattice-based post-quantum BMS construction, with a two-round signing protocol secure under concurrent sessions and signatures syntactically compatible with Raccoon under the sum of the signers' verification keys. 2026/2869.title: From Dependent Ciphertexts to Sharp Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV
2026/2869.abstract: A central challenge in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is the selection of ciphertext moduli, which depends on accurately estimating noise growth during homomorphic evaluation. Choosing excessively large moduli reduces the efficiency and scalability of the scheme, whereas underestimating noise can result in decryption failures and potential security vulnerabilities. Average-case analyses have provided promising probabilistic estimates of noise growth in practical FHE computations. 2026/2868.title: Bulletproofs are Optimal: Lower Bounds for Vector Commitments from Fiat-Shamir in Pairing-Free Groups
2026/2868.abstract: Vector Commitments allow parties to commit to an (ordered) vector and to later succinctly open it at any desired position. In plain (i.e., known order and pairing-free) prime-order groups, all state-of-the-art constructions rely on the combination of a generalized Pedersen commitment and an inner product argument. This includes the celebrated constructions of Bootle et al. (EUROCRYPT 2016) and Bünz et al. (S&P 2018), and subsequent improvements. 2026/2867.title: Collision Attacks on SHA-2: 39-Step SHA-256 below the Birthday Bound
2026/2867.abstract: SHA-2 is the most widely deployed family of hash functions, and its security margin is measured by the number of steps collision attacks reach. Li et al. gave the first classical collision attack on 38-step SHA-256, with an estimated complexity of $2^{104.3}$. The challenge is to extend the attack to more steps while retaining its advantage over generic collision search. In this paper, we show that collisions for 39-step SHA-256 can be found at an estimated cost below the $2^{128}$ birthday bound. 2026/2866.title: Anamorphic NIZK: Definition, Construction and More
2026/2866.abstract: Anamorphic encryption enables covert communication despite disclosure of ordinary decryption keys~\cite{PersianoPY22}. Work on anamorphic signatures extends this capability to settings permitting only authentication and shows that Fiat-Shamir preserves anamorphism~\cite{kutylowski2023anamorphicSignatures,fiat1986prove}. However, this result assumes an already anamorphic protocol and does not by itself ensure witness privacy against the recipient, motivating anamorphism directly in non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs). 2026/2865.title: HIT: Single-Pass Inference for Single-Trace NTT Side-Channel Attacks
2026/2865.abstract: In physical implementations of the post-quantum standards ML-KEM and ML-DSA, the Number-Theoretic Transform (NTT) directly processes secret polynomials and is a primary target for single-trace side-channel key recovery. Existing Soft Analytical Side-Channel Attacks (SASCA) apply loopy Belief Propagation (BP) over cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_q$ factor graphs, where BP fails under high noise and $O(q^2)$ updates make ML-DSA infeasible. 2026/2864.title: Tightly Secure and Modular Post-Quantum TLS Handshakes
2026/2864.abstract: In the post-quantum (PQ) migration of the TLS~1.3 handshake, the classical Diffie--Hellman key exchange is replaced with a post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism (KEM). Furthermore, KEMTLS builds upon PQ TLS~1.3 by replacing signature-based authentication with KEM-based authentication. However, all existing analyses of PQ TLS~1.3 and KEMTLS incur at least quadratic reduction losses in the number of sessions, and achieving a tightly secure construction remains an open problem. 2026/2863.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
2026/2863.abstract: Reed–Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius. We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. 2026/2862.title: An improvement to the KLPT2 algorithm
2026/2862.abstract: In this short note, we present a tweak to the KLPT2 algorithm that reduces the size of the output from $O(p^{15.5})$ to $\tilde O(p^{14.5})$.Then, we show that the recent improvement by Nakagawa, Yoshizumi and Onuki to the KLPT algorithm is compatible with the Hermitian module splitting approach, further lowering the reduced degree bound to $\tilde O(p^{14})$.

2026/2861.title: $\mathsf{SVP}_\infty$ Is NP-Hard for Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals
2026/2861.abstract: We prove that exact decision-$\mathsf{SVP}$ in the coefficient $\ell_\infty$-norm is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete for principal ideals and free modules of rank two over the cyclotomic rings $R_n=\mathbb{Z}[X]/(X^n+1)$, where $n$ ranges over powers of two. For each case, we give a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from the Subset Sum problem. For an instance with $s$ positive input integers, the output lattice has dimension $O(s)$. 2026/2860.title: Delegatable Keyed-Verification Anonymous Credentials
2026/2860.abstract: Keyed-verification anonymous credentials (KVACs) are a variant of anonymous credentials (ACs) in which the issuer and the verifier are either the same entity or mutually trusted entities. Due to this design, KVACs can avoid some of the practical burdens of publicly verifiable ACs, such as requiring bilinear pairings, making them more practical in certain settings. Delegation of credentials is a powerful feature that enables applications where users, holding a credential, can delegate a restricted version of their credential to another user. 2026/2859.title: A Single-Trace Side-Channel Attack on the KpqC Digital Signature Scheme AIMer v3
2026/2859.abstract: The Korean Post-Quantum Cryptography (KpqC) competition selected AIMer, a post-quantum digital signature scheme based on the MPC-in-the-Head paradigm, as one of its final algorithms in 2025. However, detailed side-channel analysis (SCA) of AIMer remains limited, particularly for its latest version, AIMer v3. In this paper, we present, to the best of our knowledge, the first side-channel attack on AIMer v3. 2026/2858.title: Revisiting Fiat-Shamir NIZKPs and Signatures from Seed-Friendly Sigma Protocols
2026/2858.abstract: Seed-friendly sigma protocols have a small challenge space, and when compiled into NIZKP, they require parallel repetition to reduce extraction error. Fiat-Shamir proofs obtained from seed-friendly Sigma protocols can be made more compact with fixed-weight parallel repetitions, and seed-tree compression. So far, these have been presented as compression techniques for the proof size, but standard analysis of the extraction property of NIZKP still relies on the Forking Lemma and rewinding. 2026/2857.title: When One Bit Is (Almost) Enough: A Low Leakage Chosen Plaintext Side Channel Attack on AES
2026/2857.abstract: In order to thwart Side Channel Attacks (SCA) and keep secret safe, countermeasures such as masking can be implemented to hide information. However, when a defect occurs in software or in hardware, a portion of the information may still leak. If the leak is sufficient, the state-of-the-art techniques can still be performed up to a potential brute force search to cover a missing part. However, if only a short portion of the information leaks, the completion of the attack can be hard, and considered as failed. 2026/2856.title: A New Class of PRFs and Efficient VRFs from Isogeny-based Group Actions
2026/2856.abstract: Polynomial-in-exponent pseudorandom functions (Poly-style PRFs) based on group actions have recently emerged as a promising framework for post-quantum cryptography, offering compact keys and efficient verifiability. However, the security of these constructions over composite-order class groups remains poorly understood. Prior work suggested that security is governed by the largest prime factor of the group order. In this work, we show that this intuition is flawed. 2026/2855.title: DetTreeChain: Parallel Block Production on an N-ary Block Tree with Bounded Lane Divergence
2026/2855.abstract: Nakamoto-style blockchains append one block at a time to a single chain, and raising the block rate increases forking and weakens security. We present DetTreeChain, a ledger in which up to $N$ blocks are produced in parallel and placed without later merging or reordering. Blocks form an $N$-ary tree in which each block's slot follows from its parent and its lane. A locally derived Parent Queue Pool lets only two consecutive parents receive children, so lanes never drift more than one parent apart, and links between consecutive blocks of a lane make each lane a hash chain. 2026/2854.title: Homomorphism in Expectation: Leveled Homomorphic Encryption with Range-Relative Correctness
2026/2854.abstract: Lattices have dominated the development of homomorphic encryption for deep computation. We introduce $\textit{Homomorphism in Expectation (HIE)}$, a new construction showing that encrypted addition suffices for both addition and multiplication in deep real-valued computation. Given any additively homomorphic encryption scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, we construct range-relatively correct leveled homomorphic encryption for arithmetic circuits $C$ of $\textit{arbitrary}$ polynomial depth. 2026/2853.title: ASCENT: Algebraic Structured Compilation of Exact Norms for Succinct Lattice Proofs
2026/2853.abstract: Norm bounds are semantic constraints in lattice cryptography: satisfying the modular equations is not enough unless the witness also satisfies the prescribed shortness bound. Existing norm reductions either introduce slack, or rely on general sumcheck style machinery whose transcript cost grows with the witness length. We introduce a reduction-of-knowledge compiler for exact $\ell_2$-norm constraints. 2026/2852.title: A Tutorial on Oblivious Random Access Memory
2026/2852.abstract: Abstract—Oblivious RAM (ORAM) is a key technique for pro- tecting memory access patterns in systems with untrusted mem- ory, including secure processors, trusted execution environments, and multi-party computation. This article presents a tutorial overview of ORAM concepts and designs from an algorithmic and cryptographic perspective. We review the security goals and threat models underlying ORAM, describe the most popular ORAM constructions and their core mechanisms, and discuss practical considerations for implementing ORAM. 2026/2851.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
2026/2851.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. 2026/2850.title: Neural Cipher Bench: Cost and Portability of Corner-ReLU Cipher Implementation
2026/2850.abstract: Edge and Internet of Things (IoT) devices run neural networks on GPUs, neural processing units (NPUs), and microcontrollers (MCUs) through machine learning (ML) runtimes. Deep Neural Cryptography (DNC, EUROCRYPT 2026) expressed AES as a bit-exact ReLU network with fixed weights, using a corner-ReLU construction that keeps the cipher inside the affine+ReLU operators such runtimes execute. What this construction costs on edge and IoT hardware, and whether real ML backends execute it correctly, had not been measured. 2026/2849.title: γ₁₁: Unequal Triangles and Adapted References — the macadamia 0050
2026/2849.abstract: This paper settles the ninth of the ten macadamias of the series on the Hermite constant in dimension 11: the perfect form $P$ = 0050:024468269 of rank 9, of determinant 8192/9 at minimum 4. The root paper reduces $\gamma_{11}$ to chains $L\supset M\supset N$ of lattices of ranks 11, 10, 9, each with minimum at least 4; we prove that every admissible chain whose rank-9 member is admissibly marked by $P$ has $\det L\ge 972$. 2026/2848.title: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in under 3 ms on CPU
2026/2848.abstract: This paper introduces TUTTI, a new CKKS bootstrapping procedure that outperforms previous low-latency solutions in multi-threaded latency for any number of messages and, most notably, has a lower latency than TFHE when bootstrapping a single one. Our bootstrapping builds upon SPRU (CK, TCHES 2027), improving it with new methods for exploiting parallelism and increasing the number of messages, as well as with a refined security analysis, of independent interest, of the block-binary secret keys of LMSS (AsiaCCS 2023). \tutti bootstraps $4096$ real-number messages in $46$ to $83.4$ ms on $192$ th

2026/2847.title: Access Cost Tradeoffs in Mixed-Mode Oblivious RAM
2026/2847.abstract: A mixed-mode oblivious RAM (ORAM) lets each memory request be marked public or private: public requests disclose their addresses, private requests hide them. We ask how much work such a scheme must do, and which requests must do it, in the cell-probe model—with a passive server that only reads and overwrites addressed words. We examine the expected amortized per-request cost on randomized workloads with independent modes and uniformly random addresses. 2026/2846.title: The isodual constant of the LLL potential: exact values and structure
2026/2846.abstract: The LLL potential $\Psi^2(B)=\prod_k\det\mathrm{Gram}(b_1,\dots,b_k)$, minimized over the bases of a lattice $L$ and normalized by its determinant, defines an isodual lattice invariant $\eta(L)$. Its supremum $\eta_n$ over $n$-dimensional lattices, introduced in ePrint 2007/105, is the staircase case of the generalized Hermite constants of Watanabe and Meyer, for which explicit values were known only for $n\le4$. 2026/2845.title: On Composing Oracle Separations
2026/2845.abstract: Black-box separations constitute very powerful technical barriers against constructing primitives from specific building blocks. However, they give surprisingly little indication on the usefulness of \emph{combining} several such building blocks in a single construction. We propose a set of technical conditions, under which (fully) black-box separations compose with each other. That is, if two black-box separations $P_1 \stackrel{BB}{\nRightarrow} Q$ and $P_2 \stackrel{BB}{\nRightarrow} Q$ satisfy our conditions, then $Q$ is also separated from black-box combinations of $P_1$ and $P_2$. 2026/2844.title: Antipodal necessity for rotation symmetric bent functions of degree at most three
2026/2844.abstract: The conjecture that every homogeneous rotation symmetric bent Boolean function has degree two remains open in general. We prove a necessary condition that settles the degree-three case of this conjecture. Let $n>0$ be even. If a rotation symmetric Boolean function of degree at most three in $n$ variables is bent, then its algebraic normal form contains the antipodal quadratic orbit $\sum_{i<n/2} x_i x_{i+n/2}$. 2026/2843.title: Adaptively Secure (Threshold) Batched IBE from Static Assumptions
2026/2843.abstract: Batched identity-based encryption (batched IBE) lets a key authority release one short decryption key for a set of identities and a batch label/epoch. It has been used to mitigate maximal extractable value (MEV) attacks on public blockchains. Existing constructions either use the generic-group and/or random-oracle models, or rely on $q$-type assumptions whose size grows with the batch-size bound. In this paper, we present the first adaptively secure batched IBE scheme from static assumptions. 2026/2842.title: Enabling Memory Encryption Using Ascon Derivatives
2026/2842.abstract: Keeping data stored in memory confidential is a tough challenge when assuming an adversary with physical access to it. First, we have fine-grained access to typically 256 to 512 bits at once, so nonces or tags of the typical sizes used for authenticated encryption would lead to a sizeable overhead. Second, we have stringent performance requirements, including low latency that directly impacts CPU performance and, more generally, strict area and energy constraints, especially for the high bandwidth of memory interfaces. 2026/2841.title: SEC: One-Share Everywhere-Short Secret Sharing from Lossless Expanders
2026/2841.abstract: We introduce \(\mathsf{SEC}\), an expander-code-based ramp secret sharing scheme over \(\mathbb{Z}\)-modules, particularly suitable for lattice-based distributed cryptography. It is everywhere-short: bounded secret coefficients yield bounded share coefficients, and the integer reconstruction vectors have bounded entries. Moreover, each participant receives exactly one share, regardless of the number of parties and the privacy and reconstruction thresholds. 2026/2840.title: MPCTM: MPC-Based Trajectory Matching on Unmanned Autonomous Systems
2026/2840.abstract: Emerging technologies such as Unmanned Autonomous Systems (UASs) are increasingly being deployed across several application domains. Their deployment, however, introduces safety risks, especially when unmanned vehicles operate in shared operational spaces (e.g., air, land, or maritime) and may follow collision-prone paths. This creates the need for solutions that can detect possible collisions among pre-planned trajectories, thereby improving operational safety and reducing risk. 2026/2839.title: Practical Confidential Clustering for Federated Learning using Efficient Secret-Sharing
2026/2839.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) often suffers from statistical heterogeneity, where diverging data distributions prevent a single global model from achieving high utility for all participants. Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) addresses this problem by grouping similar clients to train personalized sub-models, yet performing such clustering while ensuring strict confidentially with minimal communication overhead remains a significant challenge. 2026/2838.title: DKG: A Dual-Layer Knowledge Graph and LLM Co-Driven Framework for Fully Automated Side-Channel Analysis of Cryptosystems
2026/2838.abstract: Cryptographic algorithms underpin billions of devices, from payment smartcards to smartphone secure enclaves and industrial controllers. Yet their physical implementations risk leaking secret keys. Non-profiled side-channel analysis (SCA) evaluates whether such leakage enables key recovery, but executing it end-to-end remains expert-intensive. Large language model (LLM) agents now automate complex workflows across many domains, yet reliable key recovery requires specialized SCA knowledge that must be extracted and organized from scattered technical literature. 2026/2837.title: Adaptive Leaky LWE and Its Security
2026/2837.abstract: The Leaky LWE problem, proposed by Lai, Swarnakar, and Woo (CiC '25), studies whether LWE samples remain pseudorandom in the presence of noisy linear information about their secrets and errors. In Leaky LWE, the leakage matrix may depend on the public matrix, but must be chosen before the LWE challenge is revealed. We study $t$-round adaptive Leaky LWE, where each leakage matrix may depend on the challenge and all preceding leakage answers. 2026/2836.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
2026/2836.abstract: We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). 2026/2835.title: Multi-Hop Functional Encryption
2026/2835.abstract: In this paper, we initiate the study of multi-hop functional encryption ($\mathsf{MHFE}$), a new primitive for computing over encrypted data in recursive and multi-stage workflows while enabling controlled release of intermediate outputs. $\mathsf{MHFE}$ supports dynamic directed-acyclic computation graphs in which each node is labeled by a function and is equipped with a restricted secret key that reveals only that node's output, yet the computation can continue downstream on a forwardable encrypted state. 2026/2834.title: Undine: Distributed Extendable Merkle Tree Storage with Private Retrieval and Efficient Reconfiguration
2026/2834.abstract: Clients of transparency logs, public-key directories, and shielded blockchain pools require authenticated access to an ever-changing Merkle tree, without storing it in full or revealing which entry they open. We seek to distribute storage and query work across independent servers as the data grows and participants join, leave, change their shares, or misbehave. 2026/2833.title: The Closest Vector Problem on Gadget Lattices: Efficient Algorithms and Voronoi Geometry
2026/2833.abstract: Gadget lattices are a prominent family of lattices widely used in lattice-based cryptography, error-correcting codes, and computational complexity. We present efficient algorithms for the Closest Vector Problem (CVP) on power and CRT gadget lattices and their duals, handling arbitrary real-valued target vectors. 2026/2832.title: An Agile Homomorphic Encryption and ML-KEM Scheme for Privacy-Preserving Health Data Processing
2026/2832.abstract: The storage and processing of health data raise serious privacy con- cerns; therefore, the data must be encrypted. 2026/2828.abstract: The root paper of this series reduces $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ to a statement about chains of lattices $L\supset M\supset N$ of ranks 11, 10 and 9, cut along shortest dual vectors, whose rank-9 member lies over one of 4 487 813 perfect forms. 2026/2827.abstract: The root paper of this series reduces the value $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ of the Hermite constant to a statement about chains of lattices $L\supset M\supset N$ of ranks 11, 10 and 9 whose rank-9 member lies, in the sense of Voronoi, over one of 4 487 813 perfect forms; the $\gamma_{11}$ paper excludes all of them but ten, the macadamias. 2026/2826.title: A Focus on Hermite Constant 11
2026/2826.abstract: This paper assembles the dimension-eleven argument in a series on the Hermite constants in dimensions ten, eleven and twelve. The root paper reduces a hypothetical lattice of minimum 4 and determinant below 972 to a chain of sections of ranks eleven, ten and nine. Its rank-nine section is marked by a perfect form below an explicit determinant cutoff. The global finite computation leaves 4 487 813 candidate forms and excludes all but ten by certificates. 2026/2825.title: The Hermite Constants in Dimensions 10, 11 and 12
2026/2825.abstract: This paper introduces a series of seven papers establishing $\gamma_{10}^{10}=4^{10}/768$, $\gamma_{11}^{11}=4^{11}/972$ and $\gamma_{12}=4/\sqrt{3}$, under the attributed classification of perfect forms of rank nine and the explicitly stated computational inputs. The argument treats the dimensions in order. In dimension ten, a section orthogonal to a shortest dual vector is compared with a perfect form. 2026/2824.title: Incrementally Verifiable Oracle Aided Computation
2026/2824.abstract: Incrementally verifiable computation ($\IVC$) allows a prover to maintain a short proof that can be efficiently updated after each computation step, without retaining or recomputing the preceding execution. In the context of AI safety, the need for incremental verification is particularly important, as AI systems interact with users over time and perform further computation after each interaction. However, standard $\IVC$ schemes do not directly address a crucial feature of AI tasks: their dependence on external information and expertise. Indeed, the UK AISI Alignment Team~\cite{IrvingM25} emp

2026/2823.title: Revisiting the Security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF
2026/2823.abstract: We revisit the security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF and identify two independent security flaws. First, we establish a mask-compensation relation between continuation and termination processing in OleF and t-OleF. Exploiting this relation, we construct a two-encryption-query distinguisher against OleF with advantage $1 − 2^{−2n}$ . We further give two concrete AXU hash families for which the same attack applies to t-OleF, revealing flaws in the original DOSPRP and SPRTOP security proofs. We extend these attacks to OlÆF through valid encodings, breaking its privacy and integrity. In particular, t

2026/2822.title: Threshold Batched Attribute-Based Encryption from Succinct LWE
2026/2822.abstract: Batched identity-based encryption (BIBE) enables a single compact key to decrypt ciphertexts associated with a designated batch of identities. Batched attribute-based encryption (B-ABE) extends this functionality to attribute-based access control, while threshold batched attribute-based encryption (TB-ABE) further distributes the decryption capability among multiple parties. Existing constructions of TB-ABE rely on bilinear pairings, motivating post-quantum alternatives. In this work, we give, to the best of our knowledge, the first lattice-based candidate construction of TB-ABE. Our construct

2026/2821.title: Designing Quantum-Safe Network Architectures via Certified Randomness Distribution
2026/2821.abstract: We propose an alternative design for quantum-safe network architectures, based on distributing certified randomness generated by different trust-level QRNGs. Our modular methodology aggregates high-trust entropy from upper network layers with local contributions, enhancing the security guarantees of locally available random sequences. Leveraging the physical guarantees of QRNGs and symmetric-key cryptographic algorithms for node authentication, our approach enables immediately deployable, quantum-safe infrastructures. Such a paradigm bypasses the practical security limitations of current QKD-b

2026/2820.title: The Minimum Bucket Capacity for Reliable Path ORAM
2026/2820.abstract: Path ORAM hides memory access patterns by storing $N$ data blocks in a binary tree whose buckets have capacity $Z$, using a client-side stash for blocks that cannot be placed in the tree. Smaller buckets reduce storage and communication costs but increase the risk of stash overflow. The revised Path ORAM analysis in 2014 established an exponentially decreasing stash overflow probability for $Z \geq 5$. Experiments suggest small stashes at $Z=4$ and substantially larger ones at $Z=3$. However, it remained unknown whether $Z=4$ admits a uniform exponential stash bound or whether such a bound is

2026/2819.title: How to Revoke Users in Encryption Schemes?
2026/2819.abstract: Revocation is essential for keeping encryption secure as keys leak, devices are compromised or users leave the system. We revisit the problem of revocation for encryption schemes and give, to our knowledge, the first approach combining anonymous, collusion-resistant revocation with unchanged keys and access rules, succinct ciphertext overhead and a trustless revocation authority, i.e. that cannot decrypt. Revoking a user publishes one random-looking pseudonym, without telling encryptors whose key was revoked. A party can decrypt future ciphertexts only if it is unrevoked and satisfies the orig

2026/2818.title: Round-Optimal Statistical Verifiable Secret Sharing with Polynomial Complexity
2026/2818.abstract: Verifiable secret sharing (Chor, Goldwasser, Micali, and Awerbuch; FOCS'85) is a central primitive in secure computation, and its round complexity has been studied extensively. Rabin and Ben-Or [STOC'89] established the feasibility of statistical security up to $t<n/2$ corruptions, and Patra, Choudhary, Rabin, and Rangan [Crypto'09] showed that three sharing rounds are necessary. The work of Applebaum, Kachlon and Patra [STOC'23] introduced the first round-optimal VSS with three rounds of sharing and one round for reconstruction, albeit with exponential communication in the number of parties.

2026/2817.title: From Degree Three to Degree Two: Statistical Randomized Encodings for All Functions
2026/2817.abstract: A randomized encoding represents a function by a simpler randomized map whose output allows recovery of the function value while revealing essentially no further information about the input. Perfectly correct and perfectly private encodings of degree three over $\F_2$ are known for every Boolean function, but degree two cannot provide these guarantees for all functions (Ishai and Kushilevitz, FOCS 2000 and ICALP 2002). 2026/2816.title: SoK: Understanding Virtual Machines over Fully Homomorphic Encryption
2026/2816.abstract: We survey the current literature on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) from a virtual machine (VM) perspective. We observe that programs behave in an intrinsically different way over FHE than on plaintext, forming a new paradigm of computation that is fundamentally constrained by the obliviousness of data. To better understand the computational properties, we compile more than 125 works to formulate a cross-layer systematic view of FHE VMs, with a special focus on understanding the concrete programming models over encrypted data. In particular, we identify three distinct forms of VMs over FHE,

2026/2815.title: Jazzline: Composable CryptoLine Functional Correctness Proofs for Jasmin Programs
2026/2815.abstract: Jasmin is a programming language for high-speed and high-assurance cryptography. Correctness proofs of Jasmin programs are typically carried out deductively in EasyCrypt. This allows generality, modularity and composable reasoning, but does not scale well for low-level architecture-specific routines. CryptoLine offers a semi-automatic approach to formally verify algebraically-rich low-level cryptographic routines. CryptoLine proofs are self-contained: they are not integrated into higher-level formal verification developments. This paper shows how to soundly use CryptoLine to discharge subgoals

2026/2814.title: Registration-based Encryption with Logarithmic Registration
2026/2814.abstract: Registration-based encryption (RBE) preserves IBE's identity-only encryption interface while eliminating key escrow: users generate their own keys, and a Key Curator manages only registered public keys. However, this design introduces a new challenge: user registration, since every joining user rrequires KC to update the registry. Although theoretical RBE constructions achieve polylogarithmic registration, they rely on costly cryptographic techniques and remain impractical. 2026/2813.title: Overcoming Padding in Cryptography via Hardness of Certifying Random Strings
2026/2813.abstract: Modern cryptography relies on a provable security paradigm where the security of a primitive is established from the intractability of one or more computational problems. Hybrid arguments are central to this approach. Somewhat unexpectedly, many security proofs in the literature that use this methodology require hybrids with description-size larger than the real scheme. To argue security, the real scheme is artificially padded to match this size. 2026/2812.title: Constructions of Boolean Correctors with Optimal Nonlinearity and Vectorial Correctors Beyond Optimal Linear Correction Order
2026/2812.abstract: Correctors are postprocessing functions that reduce or eliminate statistical bias in raw bitstreams produced by physical noise sources in true random number generators. In this paper, we develop a framework based on binary Krawtchouk polynomials for analyzing and constructing Boolean and vectorial correctors. This framework reformulates the Walsh-layer criterion into finite moment constraints on support-layer counts and preimage-layer counts. 2026/2811.title: More Keys, Less Commitment: Key-Committing Attacks on BBB Accordions via Encode-then-Encipher and a Key-Committing Transform
2026/2811.abstract: Cryptographic accordions with beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security are being actively studied in connection with NIST’s ongoing standardization effort. We show that BBB security of an accordion does not necessarily strengthen key commitment of AE built from it: in many BBB accordions, additional keys introduced for BBB security give an adversary extra degrees of freedom. Exploiting this observation, we present $O(1)$ key-committing attacks on a broad range of AE schemes built from BBB accordions, mostly via the Encode-then-Encipher (EtE) paradigm, including CHCTR2, eCTR-based accordions, THCTR

2026/2810.title: QUASI: Post-Quantum Quorum Attestation of Pre-Validated Statements
2026/2810.abstract: We present QUASI, a newly conceived class of hash-based, post-quantum-secure protocols that enable a group of parties to produce a publicly verifiable attestation about a pre-validated statement. QUASI produces attestations that reduce the size and verification cost to a fraction of a full hash-based signatures collection, without relying on SNARKs or a trusted setup. QUASI rests on a surprising discovery: each party need not sign the entire statement. Authenticating only a small subset of symbols suffices for a quorum to attest to the whole. We turn this insight into a randomized construction

2026/2809.title: Pastel: Single Secret Leader Election with Private Weights
2026/2809.abstract: A single secret leader election (SSLE) protocol allows an election of exactly one leader among $n$ parties in a secrecy-preserving manner, where only the elected leader knows it has won until it publicly announces and claims leadership. Motivated by proof-of-stake blockchains where stakes are stored in an encrypted or committed form for the sake of privacy, we design and implement the first SSLE protocol with private weights. 2026/2808.title: An improved algorithm to solve the isogeny problem in dimension 2 with precomputation
2026/2808.abstract: We give a new algorithm for the superspecial isogeny problem in dimension $2$. After a one-time precomputation depending only on $p$ (which succeeds with overwhelming probability), each instance is solved in expected time and memory $p^{3/4+o(1)}$. This result is unconditional, relying on no heuristics. Including the precomputation, a single instance is solved in time $p^{19/23+o(1)}$, improving on the $p^{1+o(1)}$ of the Costello-Smith algorithm. 2026/2807.title: FirstSwap: Pre-Consensus Trade Approvals for Decentralized Market Design
2026/2807.abstract: Decentralized exchanges typically give traders no execution guarantee until a block is finalized. In the meantime, external prices move, traders strategically delay submission, and block producers can influence inclusion and ordering. We introduce FirstSwap, a DEX built on a constant-function market maker pricing curve that gives traders an early pre-approval before consensus, guaranteeing inclusion and execution within their submitted price limit, with final ordering determined by limit prices rather than by a block producer. 2026/2806.title: On Proximity Gaps for Expander Codes
2026/2806.abstract: Proximity gaps describe a phenomenon concerning random linear combinations of words and their distance from a linear error-correcting code. Informally, they address the following question: if a collection of words is jointly far from the code, is a random linear combination of those words likely to also remain far from the code? Motivated by applications to concretely efficient proof systems, in this note we study this question for expander codes, a class of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. 2026/2805.title: SNARKs from LWE via Non-black-box Reductions
2026/2805.abstract: We construct the first succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs) from the polynomial-hardness of Learning with Errors (LWE) for a subclass of UP languages whose witness unambiguity has a polynomial-size Extended Frege ($\mathcal{EF}$) proof. Our construction achieves the following soundness guarantee: For any fixed sequence of false instances $\{x_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\mathbb{N}}$, there exists a (non-constructive) constant $c>0$ such that, whenever the uniform random CRS length exceeds $\lambda^c$, the construction achieves infinitely-often soundness for this sequence $\{x_\lam

2026/2804.title: Actively Secure PIR from Verifiable Linear Relations over Rings
2026/2804.abstract: Privately retrieving data from a database without revealing which element is being retrieved is a fundamental problem in cryptography with many diverse applications. State-of-the-art solutions to this problem are generally based on homomorphic encryption, which offers security only against passive adversaries. In this work, we contribute to the recently introduced notion of Verifiable Private Information Retrieval (vPIR), which leverages verifiable computation to achieve security against active adversaries. We present a new sum-check based interactive oracle proof for linear relations over pow

2026/2803.title: The GGM PRF Construction is Optimal
2026/2803.abstract: We study the complexity of fully black-box constructions of pseudorandom functions (PRFs) from pseudorandom generators (PRGs). The seminal work of Goldreich, Goldwasser, and Micali (JACM 1986), combined with Levin’s domain-extension technique, yields PRFs that make a superlogarithmic number of adaptive calls to a length-doubling PRG. 2026/2802.title: Filtered merges make deeper representation trees pay: Subset Sum and Meet-LWE
2026/2802.abstract: Dubiner's bucketing codes, used as type-class filters on representation coordinates, let a merge avoid generating matched pairs with the wrong split pattern. We show that in representation trees their main effect is to make depth pay. For random density-one Subset Sum they improve the exponent of Bonnetain, Bricout, Schrottenloher and Shen from 0.2831 (our recomputation) to 0.2690, at depth 5; no better point was found up to depth 9. 2026/2801.title: Parallelizable modes for duplex-based authenticated encryption
2026/2801.abstract: This note enriches the SHAKE and TurboSHAKE-based authenticated encryption schemes defined by Daemen et al. at EuroS&P 2025 with parallelizable ones, while keeping their security properties. The main contribution is a new deck cipher mode, called FlightDeck, that has the ability of processing input strings similarly to KangarooTwelve and producing output strings as in counter mode, so both parallelizable. 2026/2800.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
2026/2800.abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. 2026/2799.title: Exploring the Set of APN Functions
2026/2799.abstract: An Almost Perfect Nonlinear (APN) function $F : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ provides optimal protection against differential attacks, meaning that the equation $F(x+a)=F(x)+b$ has at most 2 solutions~$x$ when $a \neq 0$. Setting aside some sporadic examples, such functions are hard to find in practice, and whether there exists APN bijections of $ \mathbb{F}_2^n$ when $n > 6$ is even (the Big APN Problem) is still unknown. 2026/2798.title: More Salt, Please: A Simple Compiler for Post-Quantum Strong aPAKE
2026/2798.abstract: Resistance to precomputation attacks is a central security goal in password-based cryptography, as it drastically increases the runtime of brute-force attacks on breached password hashes. Strong asymmetric password-authenticated key exchange (saPAKE), which enforces such precomputation resistance, is standardized by the IRTF and deployed today at large scale. Unfortunately, no practical and easy-to-deploy saPAKE exists yet that withstands quantum attackers. 2026/2797.title: The Maximum Possible Nonlinearity for a Balanced Boolean Function in 10 Variables is 492
2026/2797.abstract: Determining the maximum nonlinearity of 10-variable balanced Boolean functions has been a long-standing open problem. In this paper, we resolve it by proving that the maximum nonlinearity is exactly 492, thereby confirming Dobbertin’s conjecture in dimension 10. To exclude nonlinearity 494, we derive a quadratic residue for the Walsh spectrum and refine a local energy table from four-block concatenation by retaining the signs of the Walsh coefficients. The resulting bounds exclude all but the largest polar rank; a product inequality and a parity argument eliminate the remaining case.

2026/2796.title: Applying Combinatorial Techniques To Find Minimal Non-Complete Set Coverings
2026/2796.abstract: One of the most prominent hardware countermeasures against side-channel attacks are threshold implementations (TIs). The technique uses masking to split the operations in a cryptographic algorithm into several ones operating on shares. The coverage and non-completeness requirements of TIs are mathematically described by the notion of non-complete set coverings (NCSCs). Importantly, the number of members inside an NCSC determines the number of output shares and therefore directly impacts the complexity of the resulting TI. 2026/2795.title: Exploiting Matrix-Vector Multiplication in AIMer: Single-Trace Attacks on Key Generation and Signing
2026/2795.abstract: This paper presents two side-channel attacks against AIMer v3.0, one of the two signature schemes selected in the Korean Post-Quantum Cryptography (KpqC) competition. Both are single-trace attacks that recover the full secret key without a profiling phase, one against key generation and one against signing. 2026/2794.title: BeaverDam: A Post-Quantum Threshold Key Recovery Protocol from a One-Time Threshold Oblivious Random Function
2026/2794.abstract: Secure backups are a practical necessity of E2EE messaging apps, typically relying on password-protected key-recovery (PPKR) protocols. These allow users to turn a human-memorable password into a cryptographic key with the help of a server. Recently, Signal and Juicebox proposed threshold PPKR (tPPKR) protocols, removing the trust on a centralized server. Unfortunately, known solutions are only classically secure, lagging behind the shift toward post-quantum (PQ), or to be more precise, hybrid secure E2EE. 2026/2793.title: Weights Come Almost for Free in Ramp Threshold Cryptography
2026/2793.abstract: A weighted threshold access structure assigns a weight to each party and authorizes a subset of parties whenever their total weight exceeds a prescribed threshold. Most existing approaches to designing multiparty cryptographic protocols in the weighted threshold setting, however, either incur complexity that grows with the total weight assigned to the parties or remain far from concretely efficient. 2026/2792.title: Independent Leakage Does Not Save Evasive LWE: Refuting Folklore Fixes in the Private-Coin Setting
2026/2792.abstract: The evasive learning with errors (evasive LWE) assumption has enabled a wide range of advanced cryptographic constructions from lattices in the past few years. The simple intuition that LWE remains secure even when additional ``non-zeroizing'' short preimages are given has proved highly versatile in applications. Unfortunately, recent counterexamples have refuted its general private-coin formulations, showing that having the short preimages along with arbitrary auxiliary leakage about the secret and target matrices can invalidate this intuition. 2026/2791.title: New Results in Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption and Succinct Computational Secret Sharing from Standard Lattices
2026/2791.abstract: Projective pseudorandom generators (PPRGs), introduced by [Applebaum et al.; STOC'23], expand a short seed into a long pseudorandom string, with a special feature that one can generate a short $\textit{projected}$ key, for any set $S$, such that it reveals the output bits in $S$ while preserving pseudorandomness of the remaining bits. They demonstrated that PPRGs can bypass the 'representation size barrier' in computational secret sharing schemes, and designed PPRGs assuming hardness of a variety of standard cryptographic assumptions. 2026/2790.title: Vector Commit-and-Reduce Schemes
2026/2790.abstract: Hash-based argument systems are seeing increasing adoption in practice, owing to their ease of deployment, fast provers, and plausible post-quantum security. However, they still lag behind elliptic-curve counterparts due to their large proof sizes and (comparatively more) expensive verifiers. Attempts to optimize these metrics have focused on one of the two ingredients underlying these arguments, namely Interactive Oracle Reductions, leaving the other ingredient, Vector Commitments (VC) schemes largely ignored. 2026/2789.title: SETH: Subcode Equivalence in the Head
2026/2789.abstract: The Multi-Party Computation in the Head (MPCitH) paradigm has proven to be a versatile tool to design post-quantum digital signature schemes. Recently, MPCitH was improved with Threshold Computation in the Head (TCitH) and Vector Oblivious Linear Evaluation in the Head (VOLEitH). In this paper, we propose two polynomial models for the Subcode Equivalence Problem (SEP) and derive TCitH and VOLEitH signatures from them. 2026/2788.title: Differentially Private Distance-Sensitive Representations for General Metrics
2026/2788.abstract: A distance-sensitive set representation stores a set $S$ from a metric space $(U,d)$ and answers queries of the form "is some element of $S$ within distance $r$ of $q$?''. Existing differentially private constructions are confined to Hamming space, because they route the query through a signature map built for that metric. 2026/2787.title: Symbolic forward secrecy analysis of ML-KEM
2026/2787.abstract: Post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs) rely on generic transformations to achieve active security. Specifically, ML-KEM (FIPS 203) applies the Fujisaki--Okamoto (FO) transform to a lattice-based public-key encryption scheme, Kyber.CPAPKE, to construct an IND-CCA2 secure key exchange protocol, ML-KEM. 2026/2786.title: Quantum Key Exchange from Public Quantum Money
2026/2786.abstract: Two-message quantum key exchange (2QKE) cannot be realized in a statistically secure way, and therefore some computational assumptions are required [Malavolta and Walter 2024]. So far, the known weakest assumption for 2QKE is the existence of one-way functions (OWFs): Malavolta and Walter constructed (even everlasting-secure) 2QKE from OWFs [Malavolta and Walter 2024], and Kitagawa, Morimae, Nishimaki, and Yamakawa constructed quantum public-key encryption (QPKE) with quantum public keys, which implies 2QKE, from OWFs [Kitagawa, Morimae, Nishimaki and Yamakawa 2024]. 2026/2785.title: Optimal Early-Stopping Broadcast via Exponential Information Gathering
2026/2785.abstract: Early-stopping broadcast protocols guarantee termination based on the actual number of malicious parties, $f \leq t$, encountered during execution, rather than the worst-case scenario of $t < n$ corruptions. The seminal work of Dolev, Reischuk, and Strong~[JACM'90] established that $\min\{f+2,\, t+1\}$ rounds are necessary. 2026/2784.title: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Institutional Clinical Prediction via Multiparty Encrypted Newton-CG Logistic Regression
2026/2784.abstract: Multi-institutional clinical prediction can benefit from larger and more diverse patient populations, but privacy and data-governance constraints often prevent pooling patient-level records. This study aims to enable collaborative logistic-regression training while keeping such records local. We developed a framework combining multiparty Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) homomorphic encryption with Newton–conjugate gradient optimization. 2026/2783.title: Bridging Correlation Measures and Unpredictability: Sharp Bounds and Insights for TRNG Validation
2026/2783.abstract: Do small correlations certify high unpredictability? We answer this for the high-order correlation measures (Mauduit and Sárközy) and finite-memory sources. 2026/2782.title: Memory-Efficient HQC Implementations on Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M7
2026/2782.abstract: In the Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC) key encapsulation mechanism (KEM), eliminating the polynomial product buffer still leaves serialized inputs, operands, and candidate ciphertexts that may coexist during decapsulation. 2026/2781.title: Exact $\ell_p$-CVP via Euclidean SVP in Polynomial Space

2026/2780.title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
2026/2780.abstract: Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett–Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting. We establish the quantum analogue: if $\mathsf{UP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, then $\mathsf{NP}^{O}\cap\mathsf{coNP}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ with probability $1$ over a random oracle $O$. Beyond extending the classical result, this separat

2026/2779.title: Optimizations and First-Order Masking of AIMer on Cortex-M4
2026/2779.abstract: We optimize AIMer-128f on Cortex-M4 and propose first-order masking of its signing. Since squaring is a Frobenius map about $\times 16$ cheaper than multiplication, we restructure AIM2's inverse-Mersenne S-box into a Frobenius-shifted addition chain, cutting multiplications per S-box from 24/23 to 9/10. Since one multiplication-check operand is constant across $N = 16$ parties, we build the partial-product table once and reuse it. Both are orthogonal to single-multiplication acceleration, and with a Radix-16 multiplier on NUCLEO-L4R5ZI, keygen/sign/verify drop 18.55%/3.94%/7.30%. 1-PINI gadget

2026/2778.title: Breaking $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ via Adaptive Neuron Clustering in Cryptanalytic Model Extraction
2026/2778.abstract: Cryptanalytic model extraction poses a fundamental threat to deep learning model confidentiality by enabling precise parameter recovery with theoretical guarantees of functional equivalence. To counter this growing threat, $\mathsf{Train to Defend}$ (NeurIPS 2025) was proposed as the first dedicated defense against cryptanalytic extraction and remains the only defense believed to be effective to date. It encourages neurons to learn similar weights so that they switch activation states together, making their individual contributions harder to distinguish. However, we notice that neurons with si

2026/2777.title: Tamper-Resilient Quantum Key Encapsulation with Coherent Ciphertexts from qOWFs in the QROM
2026/2777.abstract: Kitagawa et al. (CRYPTO 2024) constructed the first tamper-resilient, chosen-ciphertext-secure public-key encryption from quantum-secure one-way functions (qOWFs). However, their construction assumes authenticated classical channels and measures intermediate signed-phase states to produce classical ciphertexts. Therefore we ask whether coherent quantum ciphertexts can support active security and certified deletion over unauthenticated classical and quantum channels. We construct the first tamper-resilient quantum key-encapsulation mechanism (QKEM) from qOWFs with coherent quantum ciphertexts a

2026/2776.title: One-Way Functions and Local Descriptions of Random Data
2026/2776.abstract: Sample compression describes a labeled sample by retained examples and extra information from which a decoder recovers the labels. We show that estimating the length of the shortest such description of random data is hard on average if and only if one-way functions exist. As in Hirahara and Nanashima's (FOCS 2023) consistent pointwise programs, the decoder labels each sample point separately, as a hypothesis does, but in our main result the labels are random rather than given by a concept. To label a point, it sees only that point, the retained examples with one extra bit each, a program, and

2026/2775.title: Quadratic Extractors
2026/2775.abstract: A quadratic source is a random variable $X\sim\mathbb{F}_2^n$ generated by applying $n$ quadratics to a hidden uniform string. Previously, the best-known explicit extractor for this model required min-entropy roughly $k=n-\sqrt{\log n}$. In this paper, we give an explicit construction for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$. Even for the special case of $2$-local sources, where each bit of $X$ depends on two hidden uniform bits, achieving an entropy requirement below $k=\sqrt{n}$ was an important open problem. 2026/2774.title: Separating Pseudorandom Codes from Quantum Random Oracles
2026/2774.abstract: Pseudorandom codes (PRCs) combine two seemingly conflicting goals: robustness to noise and computational indistinguishability from random strings. Recent work has shown that classical symmetric-key PRCs over binary alphabets cannot be constructed from minimal cryptographic assumptions, such as one-way functions, via black-box reductions. In this work, we revisit this question in the presence of quantum computation and quantum information. We first consider pseudorandom codes with classical codewords but quantum algorithms. We prove that symmetric-key pseudorandom codes robust to Bernoulli nois

2026/2773.title: Vectorized (2, 2)-Isogenies in the Theta Model Using AVX-512 and Applications to SQIsign
2026/2773.abstract: Higher-dimensional isogenies have emerged as a powerful building block for isogeny-based cryptography, with recent protocols such as SQIsign relying on the efficient evaluation of $(2^n, 2^n)$-isogenies. Despite their attractive security and compactness properties, these schemes remain computationally expensive and improving their performance is an important step for their real-world use. In this work, we present a high-performance AVX-512 implementation of two-dimensional isogenies that effectively exploits their data-level parallelism. We develop a code generator that produces efficient AVX-

2026/2772.title: STIR/SHAKEN: A Cocktail of Cryptographic Clumsiness
2026/2772.abstract: Scams and fraudulent robocalls are rampant in the telephone system. Fraudsters often employ call spoofing to impersonate a known caller to the victim, making it difficult to detect and block the fraudster’s calls. In an effort to combat call spoofing, the U.S. government in 2019 mandated the use of a new suite of protocols called STIR/SHAKEN. In STIR/SHAKEN, providers include a cryptographically-signed assertion about the caller’s identity and other metadata in call headers. This serves both to authentically convey this metadata between providers during call routing and to provide reportable,

2026/2771.title: Can Fully Homomorphic Encryption on Public Blockchains Protect Sensitive Medical Consultations? A Security and Privacy Assessment
2026/2771.abstract: %===================================================================== \begin{abstract} People seeking care for stigmatised conditions often delay treatment because they fear exposure, yet digital health services routinely expose user data and metadata. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) now allows smart contracts on public blockchains to hold encrypted data whose decryption is governed by contract rules. This paper assesses whether this approach can protect sensitive medical consultations. We present ConfidentialCare, a prototype built on Zama's fhEVM and the Ethereum Sepolia testnet, in whic

2026/2770.title: Sumcheck bit packing
2026/2770.abstract: Circuit-based zero-knowledge proofs over large fields waste most of a field element when they commit to a single bit. We study the problem of committing to packed witnesses, in which $m$ bits are stored in one element of $GF(2^m)$, while still allowing the proof system to verify linear claims about the individual bits. Prior approaches to this problem either (a) scale to packing only 4 bits[Fs24], (b) require tensor-structured claims and additional sumcheck rounds that incur larger soundness error [DP23,DP25], or (c) rely on Frobenius automorphisms [Koc26]. 2026/2769.title: Projective Jet Geometry and Hold-Out Rank of Binary Goppa Codes
2026/2769.abstract: We develop a projective-geometric and algebraic framework for the higher-order polynomial relations among the public generator-matrix columns of a binary Goppa code, the relations exploited by the recent structural distinguishers and key-recovery methods for Classic McEliece. The alternant representation realizes the public columns as rational points on a hidden curve parametrized over $\F_{2^m}$; higher-order vanishing conditions become fat-point conditions, pulled back along the hidden parametrization. Our first contribution is an exact characterization of a codimension-$t$ ambient space con

2026/2768.title: Cryptanalysis of Pairing-Based Additive Masking with Prime-Field Secrets
2026/2768.abstract: We analyze the public values generated by a pairing-based multi-secret sharing construction in which each secret is added to a power of a common pairing value. The secrets lie in the prime subfield of the extension field containing the public values. We show that the first two public values determine the common mask whenever an explicit nonzero condition holds. We also show that the exceptional case is resolved for the parameter set considered in the numerical example. 2026/2767.title: HqcLethe: Streaming HQC Encapsulation for Tiny Stateless Servers
2026/2767.abstract: Stateless post-quantum authenticated key exchanges such as post-quantum WireGuard hedge against unexpected cryptanalytic advances by combining a lattice KEM with code-based Classic McEliece. However, recent attacks have led Germany's BSI to advise against McEliece, which leaves these protocols with lattices alone. HQC, the code-based KEM that NIST selected, could restore diversity, but its keys do not fit in a single packet, so a server would have to buffer multi-packet handshakes. 2026/2766.title: Keyber: Recovering the Signal by Amplifying the Noise in ML-KEM
2026/2766.abstract: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) is now being deployed in real-world applications to provide security against adversaries with quantum computers. Therefore, the resistance of ML-KEM’s implementations to physical attacks requires thorough evaluation. So far, fault attacks on ML-KEM have targeted the decapsulation operation. The key generation operation has received little attention from a fault-attack perspective. In this work, we present Keyber, the first statistical ineffective fault attack (SIFA) on the key generation of ML-KEM. Keyber is a key-recovery attack that needs only a single fault in key generati

2026/2765.title: BASTION: Lock-Step, Staggered and Sequential Share Schedules for a First-Order Masked ML-KEM NTT on FPGA
2026/2765.abstract: The Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is the arithmetic core of ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and a prominent side-channel target in hardware. Because the transform is linear, first-order arithmetic masking applies share-wise without fresh randomness, which leaves one design decision open: when each share is processed. Published designs process the shares in sequence on one datapath, or on one datapath per share started a configurable delay apart and in random order; running both datapaths in lock-step is the third option. 2026/2764.title: Trapdoors Beyond Inversion: Recoverable Information in Public-Key Cryptography
2026/2764.abstract: Classical trapdoor functions recover complete preimages, whereas public-key decryption needs only designated information about an encryption input. We study this distinction through trapdoor hardcore functions (TDHFs), whose trapdoor recovers a prescribed value $h(x)$ from a public evaluation $f (x)$, while $h(x)$ remains pseudorandom given the public key and evaluation. For perfectly correct primitives, we show that adaptive TDHFs characterize IND-CCA2-secure public-key encryption. 2026/2763.title: On Key Recovery from Exposed Neural XOR Activations in DES and TDES
2026/2763.abstract: We study the security of natural ReLU realizations of the Data Encryption Standard (DES) and two-key Triple DES (TDES) when an adversary can submit non-binary inputs and observe selected intermediate neural values. The attack exploits the piecewise-linear extension of XOR: paired inputs that differ in one expanded right-half bit reveal the corresponding round-key bit from the change in a natural XOR node. 2026/2762.title: AirBB: Lightweight Threshold Anonymous Credentials without Random Oracles from BB Signatures
2026/2762.abstract: Anonymous credentials are a well-studied cryptographic primitive enabling users to prove statements about their identity and selectively present personal information in an unlinkable manner. The issuer, however, is often a single point of failure. Threshold issuance addresses this by distributing the issuer across several parties such that a quorum of them must cooperate to issue credentials. Numerous constructions of single-issuer and threshold issuance anonymous credentials have been proposed. However, existing schemes each have at least one of the following weaknesses: (1) their presentatio

2026/2761.title: Superlattice methods for the shortest vector problem and discrete Gaussian sampling
2026/2761.abstract: We give worst-case algorithms for the shortest vector problem (SVP) and discrete Gaussian sampling (DGS) at arbitrary widths. Both algorithms generate lists on a dense superlattice and combine vectors along a chain down to the input lattice. Random shifts let us control the expected number of representations of a vector regardless of the lattice. For SVP we balance these counts with a novel midpoint-shell test to ensure output distributions are sufficiently uniform. 2026/2760.title: Syndrome Decoding out of the Head: Structure-Aided Side-Channel Witness Recovery on SDitH
2026/2760.abstract: Regular syndrome decoding (RSD) underlies several code-based signature schemes, including SD-in-the-Head (SDitH). Its secret witness has exactly one nonzero coordinate per block, and the selected positions must satisfy a public syndrome equation. In this work, we show how these structural constraints can be exploited to recover the complete witness from imperfect side-channel information. We present a profiled power analysis of the witness-embedding operation in the SDitH Round-3 reference implementation. 2026/2759.title: Differentially Oblivious Graph Ball Queries
2026/2759.abstract: A graph ball query returns all vertices within distance $r$ of a source vertex. On $N$-vertex graphs with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, ordinary breadth-first search answers such queries with $O_{\Delta,r}(1)$ record accesses. These accesses depend on private edges and can reveal graph structure. Full obliviousness hides this dependence, but incurs substantial overhead. Differential obliviousness (DO) [Chan et al., SODA'2019] trades off between privacy and efficiency by relaxing full obliviousness to $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differential privacy on the access traces of neighboring graphs. We

2026/2758.title: Fine-Grained Proof Complexity for Elementary Arithmetic in Extended Frege
2026/2758.abstract: Proof complexity has historically focused on qualitative results, such as whether natural mathematical statements (e.g. the Pigeonhole Principle) admit polynomial-size proofs in certain proof systems (e.g. Resolution or Frege). In contrast to the rich theory of algorithm design, there is little understanding of how to design quantitatively efficient proofs. We initiate the study of fine-grained propositional proof complexity. Our motivation comes from an emerging line of cryptographic constructions such as the elegant work of Jain and Jin (2022), in which the efficiency of the resulting scheme

2026/2757.title: Affine Advantage in Guess-type Attacks on Goldreich’s PRGs: Generalization, Characterization and Countermeasures
2026/2757.abstract: The recent guess-type attack (Eurocrypt'26) on Goldreich's pseudorandom generators exploits the strong bias toward constants that can arise when some inputs of majority-based predicates are fixed. This attack has demonstrated substantial effectiveness against several concrete parameter instances (Eurocrypt'24\&'25, Asiacrypt'24). In this paper, we generalize this attack paradigm to arbitrary affine approximations, characterize its capabilities, and develop a new predicate as a countermeasure. 2026/2756.title: Refined Bounds for the Smoothing Parameter of Lattices
2026/2756.abstract: The smoothing parameter $\eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda)$ is a fundamental invariant in lattice-based cryptography. Zheng, Zhao, and Xu (AAECC 2021) proved $\eta_\varepsilon(\mathbb{Z}) \le \sqrt{\ln(\frac{2}{\varepsilon} + \frac{\varepsilon}{44})/\pi}$ and $\eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda) \le \sqrt{\ln(n - 1 + \frac{2n}{\varepsilon})/\pi}\,\mathrm{bl}(\Lambda)$. Guo, Liu, Wang, and Tian (PLOS One 2025) proposed $\eta_\varepsilon(\mathbb{Z}) \le \sqrt{\ln(\frac{2}{\varepsilon} + \frac{\varepsilon}{m})/\pi}$ for $0 < \varepsilon \le \frac{4}{m} - \frac{172}{m^6}$ ($m \ge 3$) and $\eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda)

2026/2755.title: Blockchain-Anchored Proactive Refresh for Dynamic Threshold Services
2026/2755.abstract: A long-lived threshold service must issue shares to participants that join after deployment, refresh them against a mobile adversary, and allow participants offline during a refresh to recover missed updates. We show that charging exposure solely to committed epochs is fundamentally insufficient: an aborted refresh attempt that publishes candidate update tokens can reveal the secret even if no committed epoch exceeds its corruption budget. 2026/2754.title: A note on zero-knowledge ring switching
2026/2754.abstract: We make the ring-switching technique of Diamond and Posen zero knowledge, resolving a problem left open in the literature. Over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$, our technique uses $n-1$ auxiliary masks and $n-1$ quadratic constraints, checked in zero knowledge by the underlying commitment scheme.

2026/2753.title: Correlation Power Analysis of SHA-2-Based SLH-DSA
2026/2753.abstract: SLH-DSA repeatedly processes a fixed secret seed together with varying public addresses, making its physical implementation a target for side-channel analysis. We present non-profiled correlation power analysis (CPA) procedures for the address-based pseudorandom function in all six SHA-2-based SLH-DSA parameter sets, using SHA256 compression rounds and message-schedule expansion. The procedures include joint recovery of two partial secrets in the 256-bit parameter sets and an alternative first message-schedule step for 128-bit WOTS+ addresses. 2026/2752.title: Information Loss Is All You Need: TC⁰ Pseudorandomness from Worst-Case Lattices
2026/2752.abstract: Pseudorandomness plays a central role in algorithms, complexity theory, and cryptography. We ask whether deterministic information loss alone can yield post-quantum pseudorandomness with $\mathrm{TC}^0$ evaluation. Learning with errors (LWE) hides linear measurements with random noise. Learning with rounding (LWR) replaces noise with deterministic rounding, but a standard polynomial-modulus hardness reduction requires parameters tailored to a predetermined sample bound. 2026/2751.title: An efficient Failure Probability Estimator for LWE-based encryption, and application to IBE
2026/2751.abstract: In recent years, lattice-based cryptography has proven to be a source of post-quantum cryptosystems. In particular, the blueprint of Learning With Errors (LWE) encryption enabled the creation of Kyber, chosen by NIST to be standardized as ML-KEM. Because of the structure of LWE encryption, the decryption of a ciphertext can give an incorrect plaintext. This event (a decryption failure) happens randomly with some probability. Since this is a problem for both functionality and security, we must ensure that this failure probability is cryptographically negligible. Usually, this is assessed with t

2026/2750.title: Practical Optimal Bucket Sets with Power-of-Two Radices for LFG-Based MSM Algorithms
2026/2750.abstract: Fixed point multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) is a major computational component of pairing-based SNARK proof generation. The Luo--Fu--Gong (LFG) framework is a variant of Pippenger's bucket method that uses a multiplier set $M$ and precomputed point multiples to reduce the number of buckets and online point additions. For radix $q$ and a positive multiplier set $M$, covering all digit residues requires a bucket set of size at least $q/(2|M|)$. 2026/2749.title: Shielded Bitcoin: Private Transfers on the Bitcoin L1
2026/2749.abstract: This paper introduces Shielded Bitcoin, a protocol for private transfer of Bitcoin directly on the Bitcoin L1, requiring no changes to Bitcoin consensus. Its design borrows from the architecture of Zcash and earlier shielded-note systems: value is held as encrypted notes, spends are marked by public nullifiers, and validity is established by zero-knowledge proofs. Unlike Zcash, Shielded Bitcoin introduces no dedicated consensus chain: all protocol data is published on Bitcoin, transfer validity is enforced through PIPEs v2 [ACG+26], and shielded state is reconstructed by deterministic replay o

2026/2748.title: TFNP in the Random Oracle Model
2026/2748.abstract: We determine which major TFNP classes are hard in the random oracle model (ROM). Prior work establishes average-case hardness of highly structured subclasses of TFNP from strong cryptographic assumptions such as LWE and indistinguishability obfuscation. It is not known whether weaker assumptions such as one-way functions imply hardness of any of the standard TFNP subclasses, even in the worst case. The ROM, where all parties have query access to a random function, lies, morally, between these two regimes: a random function is one-way, but public-key cryptography cannot be built from it in a bl

2026/2747.title: MODDIV-WC: Unit-Anchored Toeplitz/Hankel Rounding with Exact Binary-LWE Masking and an IND-CCA Security Route
2026/2747.abstract: \begin{abstract} We present MODDIV-WC, a public-key encryption and key-encapsulation candidate based on a widened Hankel linear map followed by deterministic integer division, together with an implicit-rejection Fujisaki--Okamoto wrapper, MODDIV-WC-FO. The construction uses a secret vector whose first coordinate is fixed to one and whose remaining coordinates are sampled from a positive interval. This unit anchor makes the Hankel map surjective for every admissible secret, a property that is central to the proof. The security analysis has four layers. First, we give an exact embedding of binar

2026/2746.title: Differential Cryptanalysis of SPEEDY: Revised Security Evaluation and Improved Key Recovery Attack
2026/2746.abstract: The resistance of a block cipher against differential cryptanalysis (DC) is a fundamental criterion for evaluating its security. SPEEDY is a family of low-latency SPS-type block ciphers designed by Leander et al. The designers presented two evaluations of SPEEDY against DC: the first restricted 1-bit-to-1-bit differential propagations through the S-box and used the higher-order branch numbers to estimate the maximum expected differential probability (EDP) of differential trails; the second imposed a structural restriction and assumed that all 1-bit-to-1-bit propagations through an active S-box

2026/2745.title: The Price of Agreement in Secure Multiparty Computation
2026/2745.abstract: Secure multi-party computation (MPC) cannot guarantee output delivery, in general, in the dishonest-majority setting. Security of MPC is therefore relaxed to security with abort, where the adversary may prevent honest parties from obtaining their output. The standard notion of \emph{unanimous abort} (UA-MPC) ensures that either all honest parties obtain their output or all of them abort. Goldwasser and Lindell [JCRYPT '05] introduced the relaxed notion of \emph{selective abort}, allowing some honest parties to abort and others to obtain their output. While two-round SA-MPC can be achieved over

2026/2744.title: Phantom Timing Leaks on Cortex-M4: A Pre-registered Evaluation of ML-KEM Decapsulation
2026/2744.abstract: Fixed-versus-random timing tests in the style of dudect are a cheap first check of constant-time behaviour, and on microcontrollers the cycle counter makes them exact to the cycle. We report a pre-registered evaluation of ML-KEM decapsulation on an STM32F411 (Cortex-M4) covering nine implementations of PQM4 (clean, m4fspeed, m4fstack for ML-KEM-512/768/1024) and a positive control in which we restored the pre-KyberSlash division formulas. 2026/2743.title: Challenge Binding in FRESCO SPDZ2k: A Message-Level Case Study
2026/2743.abstract: FRESCO's SPDZ2k suite derives its batched MAC-check coefficients from a setup-time public seed, making the stream predictable before opening shares are sent. We examine this implementation path at a pinned revision. A source-level derivation accounts for low-limb carries and high-bit corrections and shows that the value-share shifts $e=(r_j,-r_i)$ preserve the check residual while retaining the original MAC shares. 2026/2742.title: Differentially $2^t$-uniform quadrinomials with high nonlinearity
2026/2742.abstract: In this paper, we discuss some cryptographic properties of a family of quadrinomials constructed as a generalization of a known family of APN quadrinomials. In particular, we show that this family produces differentially $2^t$-uniform quadrinomials with the same Walsh spectrum as the Gold power function $x^{2^t+1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$. We also discuss whether this family provides permutations.

2026/2741.title: Leakage-Resilient Computation via Matrix Refreshing
2026/2741.abstract: Leakage-resilient cryptography protects secrets against side-channel attacks, in which a physical implementation reveals partial information about its internal state. A fundamental primitive in this area is a leakage-resilient storage, which allows a secret to be stored in a way that remains secure even if an adversary learns some information about the storage's internal state. A popular approach represents a secret as the inner product of two $n$-bit vectors, called shares. The shares are stored and processed separately by two parts of the implementation, called the left and right parties. Be

2026/2740.title: Dual Coppersmith: Finding Small Roots Without Multivariate Polynomial Systems
2026/2740.abstract: The multivariate Coppersmith algorithm is a central tool in public-key cryptanalysis for finding a small hidden root of modular polynomial equations. It consists of two stages. First, a lattice-reduction (LR) stage constructs auxiliary equations satisfied by the hidden root over $\mathbb Z$. Second, a root-recovery (RR) stage solves these equations. 2026/2739.title: Archive Certificates for ML-DSA-87 Authorizations from an Exact Bounded Relation
2026/2739.abstract: A blockchain that signs every transaction with FIPS 204 ML-DSA-87 keeps 4,627 bytes of signature per transaction forever. We describe and measure an archive certificate: one hash-based proof, for a range of already validated blocks, of knowledge of canonical FIPS 204 signatures on exactly the recorded messages under the keys resolved from chain state. Fresh blocks keep native verification. The construction starts from an exact bounded relation for ML-DSA-87 verification once the high bits $u = w'_1$ are fixed.
