2026/2738.title: The Fairest of Them All: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Leader Election
2026/2738.abstract: Fair leader election is the problem of sampling an unbiased random party out of a set of $n$ parties. The seminal impossibility result of Cleve (STOC 1986) applies to this setting, and shows that the result of the election cannot be unbiased against a dishonest majority. Recent work has achieved the weaker property of game-theoretic fairness, where behaving dishonestly cannot improve one’s chances of being elected. However, such protocols allow even a single corrupt party to bias the outcome. In this work, we introduce best-of-both-worlds (BoBW) fairness, where a small number $t_S$ of corrupt

2026/2737.title: Leakage-Tolerant Computation without Leakage-Free Setup
2026/2737.abstract: Leakage-tolerant multi-party computation (MPC) ensures that leakage from each honest party’s internal state reveals no more than the leakage from honest parties' individual inputs and outputs, beyond the standard security guarantee of MPC. Previous constructions either require a leakage-free preprocessing, or rely on indistinguishability obfuscation in the common reference string (CRS) model and only achieve semi-honest security. 2026/2736.title: PS-BKZ: Decoupling Outer Propagation and Local Processing in BKZ by Parameter Separation
2026/2736.abstract: This work provides a systematic study of parameter separation in Block Korkine–Zolotarev (BKZ) reduction. We propose a general framework with separate parameters for outer propagation and the dominant local computation. The framework covers the local parameter settings of standard BKZ and variants using extended preprocessing, dimensions for free, or progressive sieving, with corresponding adaptations to the outer operations. This allows less expensive local processing without narrowing the outer propagation range. Within this framework, we give idealized and executable constructions that use

2026/2735.title: Perseus: A Full-Stack System for Homomorphic Model Inference
2026/2735.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made it exceptionally convenient for users to send their private data to model providers, which process them in plaintext. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) promises to secure remote inference by computing directly on encrypted data, yet it has remained prohibitively slow. The effort to make it practical remains fragmented, with most existing frameworks being closed-source, which keeps progress from compounding. We present Perseus, a free and open Python software library that supports the full stack of encrypted model inference, from the cryptographic backend

2026/2734.title: Finite-Batch q-ary OT Extension for High-Arity Private Lookup: Certified Radix--Code Co-Design
2026/2734.abstract: High-arity oblivious transfer is a natural abstraction for private lookup: a $\delta$-bit table address selects one entry out of $2^\delta$ candidates. This paper characterizes the finite-batch design space of the CCG q-ary OT-extension family and derives certified radix-selection rules. For $q=2^r$, we formulate radix-code selection as a security-constrained discrete optimization problem that accounts for subfield-check padding, code dimension, required distance, base-OT count, and q-ary symbol width. 2026/2733.title: Cryptanalysis of MinRank 2.0
2026/2733.abstract: MinRank is an NP-complete problem underlying the security of several post-quantum schemes. It is the hardness assumption of the NIST second-round signature candidate Mirath and of the encryption schemes of Chatterjee et al.\ and Debris-Alazard et al.\ at Eurocrypt 2026. Moreover, it is ubiquitous in the cryptanalysis of multivariate schemes, among them the third-round candidates UOV, MAYO, QR-UOV, and SNOVA. In this work, we revisit the attacks on MinRank. 2026/2732.title: MuCPay: Breaking the Quadratic Bottleneck in Scriptless Multi-Party Oracle-Based Conditional Payments
2026/2732.abstract: Oracle-based conditional payments triggered by real-world events support decentralized finance applications. However, dense independent bilateral deployments require $\Theta(Nn^2)$ outcome authorizations and $\Theta(n^2)$ settlement signatures for $n$ parties and $N$ outcomes. To go beyond two-party settings, we propose MuCPay, a multi-party oracle-based conditional payment protocol combining (i) $\Theta(Nn)$ off-chain signing shares with one on-chain settlement signature and (ii) BIP340-compatible scriptless settlement on Bitcoin. At its core, MuCPay introduces hash-bound adaptor multi-signat

2026/2731.title: FixSampZ: A Fixed-Point Hardware-Efficient Discrete Gaussian Sampler for Falcon Signatures
2026/2731.abstract: Falcon, a NIST-standardized post-quantum signature algorithm, offers compact signatures but relies on hardware-intensive floating-point arithmetic. Building on recent theoretical fixed-point formulations, we present a completely floating-point-free hardware architecture for SamplerZ, Falcon’s primary signing bottleneck. By utilizing zero-cost hardware bit-sliced retagging of fixed-point data, which software avoids due to instruction overheads, we enforce tighter data formats at every stage boundary without area or latency penalties. Furthermore, executing floor functions as trivial two's-compl

2026/2730.title: Kaiburr: ML-KEM at (much) higher security
2026/2730.abstract: With deployment of standardized post-quantum cryptography well on the way, discussions continue about concrete choices of schemes and parameter sets. For example, while NIST standardized structured-lattice-based ML-KEM, European agencies like BSI and ANSSI favor unstructured-lattice-based FrodoKEM. Another discussion revolves around different approaches to hybrid deployments – either combining post-quantum schemes with "traditional" elliptic-curve cryptography (or RSA) or combining multiple different post-quantum schemes. 2026/2729.title: Quotienting Redundant Tables: Practical Master-Key Recovery from WBSLT White-Box AES
2026/2729.abstract: Enlarging lookup-table addresses does not hide smaller selectors when the complete public table factors through a core with distinct rows and distinct columns. We demonstrate this condition in WBSLT, a white-box AES design presented at NDSS 2026 that reports resistance to several structural attacks. In the released general generator, the joint output of each group of four first-round TypeII tables has an exact 16 × 16 quotient of its 64 × 64 address space. Mapping its row and column classes to observed addresses recovers the original nibble partition of each AES input byte. Public tables imple

2026/2728.title: Tight Depth Lower Bounds for Stretch Amplification
2026/2728.abstract: We investigate the depth overhead of stretch-amplification for pseudorandom generators in the black-box model. We show that any black box construction of a PRG $H: \{0,1\}^m \to \{0,1\}^M$ which makes $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ queries to a PRG $G: \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^N$ in $d$ adaptive phases during each evaluation (and with a black-box reduction to the security of $G$) must satisfy: $M \leq (m + O(\log n)) \Bigl( \frac{N}{n - O(\log n)} \Bigr)^d$. This implies that the standard amplification procedure [GM'84, GGM'86] based on repeated composition of $G$ is essentially optimal. In particular, ampli

2026/2727.title: On the (Quantum) Communication Complexity of Secure MPC from a Random Oracle
2026/2727.abstract: Information-theoretic MPC among $n$ parties with $t$ corruptions can securely evaluate a circuit $C$ with $O(|C| \cdot t/(n-t))$ online communication in the preprocessing model and $O(|C| \cdot t/(n-2t))$ communication in the honest majority setting. Damg{\aa}rd, Larsen and Nielsen (CRYPTO 2019) showed that both communication bounds are tight for inner products. Fully homomorphic encryption and other assumptions known to imply public-key cryptography beat both communication bounds, but the communication complexity with symmetric-key cryptography alone is less understood. 2026/2726.title: Efficient Polynomial Multiplier Architectures for ML-KEM on Resource-Constrained FPGAs
2026/2726.abstract: The Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is a key component of polynomial multiplication in Kyber, making its efficient hardware implementation essential for post-quantum cryptographic applications. This paper presents two hardware architectures for Kyber polynomial arithmetic, supporting the NTT, inverse NTT (INTT) and point-wise multiplication (PWM) operations. The first architecture employs a single processing element (PE) to reduce hardware area, while the second uses two PEs to achieve higher throughput and efficiency. 2026/2725.title: Complete Addition Law for Twisted Edwards Curves
2026/2725.abstract: We construct complete addition laws in extended coordinates for twisted Edwards curves \(E_{a,d}:ax^2+y^2=1+dx^2y^2\), where \(a,d\in K^\times\), \(a\ne d\), and \(\operatorname{char}K\ne2\). If \(t\in K\) makes \((t^2-a)(t^2-d)\) a nonzero nonsquare, the construction yields a \(K\)-complete formula valid for every pair of \(K\)-rational points. The proof describes the exceptional fibres through the difference morphism. 2026/2724.title: Complete Addition on Short Weierstrass Curves with Point-Free Lines
2026/2724.abstract: Let $E_{a,b}:Y^2Z=X^3+aXZ^2+bZ^3$ be a nonsingular short-Weierstrass curve over a field $K$ of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. A nonvertical line $Y=mX+nZ$ has no $K$-rational point on the curve if and only if $x^3-m^2x^2+(a-2mn)x+b-n^2$ is rootless in $K$. We give coordinate changes and formulas for the corresponding $K$-complete Bosma--Lenstra addition law. An incidence count proves that such a line exists over every finite field in the stated characteristic. 2026/2723.title: Distill and Conquer: Cryptanalytic Extraction of Local Rules in the Hard-Label Setting
2026/2723.abstract: Cryptanalytic extraction can expose proprietary neural network parameters, but unknown architectures and large parameter counts complicate recovery under hard-label access. Local class-pair rules offer a narrower target by making class-switching conditions explicit and predicting nearby labels under a specified sampling law. Distillation methods mainly return substitute models rather than explicit rules whose local agreement has been tested against the victim. We propose Distill–Probe–Extract to produce such rules without first identifying the victim architecture. Verified boundary events guid

2026/2722.title: Normal-Jet Masking: A Retraining-Free Defense Against Cryptanalytic Extraction of Neural Networks
2026/2722.abstract: Cryptanalytic extraction (CEA) of piecewise-linear neural networks recovers hidden signatures and parameters by locating critical points or hard-label dual points that expose off-manifold geometry. Proposed mitigation methods include query monitoring, output perturbation, ownership verification, and extraction-aware training. Train to Defend (TTD) directly addresses CEA through extraction-aware training, but cannot protect an already-trained checkpoint without retraining. We propose Normal-Jet Masking (NJM), a post-training wrapper that leaves the source model unchanged. NJM calibrates a tange

2026/2721.title: Authenticated Outsourced Incrementally Verifiable MPC
2026/2721.abstract: Many privacy-preserving applications such as iterative machine learning training require executing ongoing computations over a secret state for long periods of time. While MPC enables secure computation, long-lived secret state is vulnerable to adaptive corruptions, requiring periodic share refreshes and committee rotation. In many settings, it is desirable for external parties to be able to verify that these state updates and rotations are performed correctly, but existing approaches for such public verifiability incur high overhead as they require MPC nodes to generate expensive proofs over

2026/2720.title: Unique Signature Schemes with Tight Security in the Random Oracle Model via Hash-and-Subset-Sign
2026/2720.abstract: Unique signatures are digital signature schemes, where each message has exactly one valid signature. The uniqueness property typically comes at a price: Most unique signature schemes are known to have a security loss at least linear in the number of signature queries when aiming for existential unforgeability under chosen message attacks (EUF-CMA) security, which was shown to be inherent in the standard model by Coron (EUROCRYPT 2002) for signature schemes where public keys are verifiable (i.e., where it can be efficiently checked whether a public key has unique signatures). 2026/2719.title: Construction and Classification of Minimum-Latency 5-Bit APN S-Boxes
2026/2719.abstract: S-boxes serve as essential nonlinear building blocks in symmetric-key cryptography, where their cryptographic properties and hardware implementation costs jointly dictate the security and efficiency of lightweight primitives. This paper studies the construction and classification of minimum-latency 5-bit APN (Almost Perfect Nonlinear) permutations under a prescribed gate-delay model, using exact minimum latencies of Boolean component functions. Under the fixed gate-delay model of the NanGate 45nm standard cell library, we partition the search space into input-variable permutation (IP) equivale

2026/2718.title: Revisiting Accountability in Accountable Tracing Signatures
2026/2718.abstract: Accountable tracing signatures (ATS), introduced by Kohlweiss and Miers (PoPETs 2015), classify each group member (user) as either traceable or non-traceable. A traceable user corresponds to one in conventional group signature schemes whose identity can be revealed by the opener from a signature, whereas a non-traceable user cannot be identified from any signature they produce. The opener, who issues a witness, can certify a user's status via the Account algorithm. 2026/2717.title: Verifiable Data on Bitcoin: FlatMerkle Commitments, Refutable Proofs, and FlatChecks
2026/2717.abstract: We give a method to publish data on Bitcoin and to verify properties of that data on Bitcoin itself, against a publisher who may lie. The data is a FlatMerkle file – a structured byte string whose ordinary SHA-256 supports logarithmic inclusion proofs and logarithmic proofs of malformation – placed in a transaction's annex or, at four times the cost but relayable by Bitcoin Core, in an output. 2026/2716.title: Key Recovery Against RLCE via the GIJS Distinguisher
2026/2716.abstract: We present an experimental cryptanalysis of the RLCE cryptosystem at the heretofore secure $w=n-k$ parameter regime. Our attack relies crucially on the recent Ghoshal--Ishai--Jain--Sun (GIJS) distinguisher The attack shortens the public key at random positions, runs the GIJS distinguisher with \emph{every} column as hold-out, and uses this distinguisher to identify twin pairs based on how they appear across trials. 2026/2715.title: A Constant-Rate Compiler for Continual Memory Leakage
2026/2715.abstract: Leakage-resilient compilers transform any computation so that physical leakage from its implementation reveals nothing beyond its input-output behaviour. In this work, we investigate this question in the well-motivated continual memory leakage (CML) model, that captures a variety of relevant real-world side-channel attacks and subsumes several other well studied models in the leakage domain. In this model with two independently leaking components (at least two are necessary), all known general compilers tolerate only an inverse-polynomial leakage-rate. 2026/2714.title: Polynomial Batch Accumulators for Onboarding-Dominant Zero-Knowledge Membership Proofs
2026/2714.abstract: Zero-knowledge membership accumulators are conventionally tailored for slowly growing sets with frequent proof generation, creating severe efficiency bottlenecks for modern compliance architectures. Governance-driven applications like FATF customer due diligence, eIDAS 2.0 wallet issuance, and MiCA VASP authorization invert this structure. In this regime, rosters are ingested at an enterprise scale, while proofs are requested selectively. To resolve this mismatch, we introduce Polynomial Equation Batching (PEB), a membership accumulator for onboarding heavy workloads. PEB represents up to 128

2026/2713.title: CHAMPing at the Bit: Short Square-Root Collisions for Two-Generator Cayley Hashes
2026/2713.abstract: For $A,B\in\text{GL}(\mathbb{F}_p)$, a Cayley hash $\text{HM}(w)$ maps a bit string $w \in \{0,1\}$ to the corresponding product of $A$ and $B$. We construct collisions by finding two palindromes whose matrix products commute. A symmetric form shared by the two generators places the hash of every palindrome in a three-dimensional subspace containing the identity. Two such hashes commute when their traceless parts are proportional, which defines a class map with $p+2$ values, so the pigeonhole principle gives collisions of $4\lceil\log_2(p+3)\rceil$ bits. 2026/2712.title: Concrete Minimum Distance Bounds of Accumulate Codes over any Fixed Finite Field
2026/2712.abstract: We present a new concrete unified distance analysis of three accumulate-type error-correcting codes over any finite field, specifically the Repeat-Accumulate (RA), Repeat-Accumulate-Accumulate (RAA), and Expand-Accumulate (EA) codes. For message length $k$, codeword length $n$, finite field size $q>2$, and target relative minimum distance $\delta$, we give new upper bounds on the probability that each of the above codes do not have minimum distance at least $\delta$. Our bounds are concrete and explicit: they do not rely on $n$ or $q$ being sufficiently large. We present (multiple) closed-form

2026/2711.title: Fast Provable Algorithms for Approximate CVP and Exact SVP on Random \(q\)-ary Lattices
2026/2711.abstract: We give provable randomized algorithms for the $\gamma$-approximate Closest Vector Problem ($\gamma$-CVP) with $\gamma=5/3$ and the exact Shortest Vector Problem (SVP) in the Euclidean norm on random $q$-ary lattices. These lattices consist of the integer vectors mapped to zero modulo $q$ by a uniformly random matrix $\mathbf{H}\in(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})^{m\times n}$, for any integer $q\ge2$. For input density $\delta=m\log_2q/n$ with $0\le\delta\le1$, the running times are $2^{0.2668n+o(n)}$ for $5/3$-CVP and $2^{0.2741n+o(n)}$ for exact SVP, with polynomial input-length factors suppressed.

2026/2710.title: Hidden Curves and Short Duals: Cubic Jets, Dual Leaks, and the Limits of Masked-Code Encryption
2026/2710.abstract: Masked-code encryption hides a decodable code behind a transformation meant to make it look random. We study the two masks proposed as compact alternatives to Goppa codes---Wang's RLCE and the $(U\,|\,U{+}V)$ construction of UVW-KEM---over the decodable hidden codes they have been or could be applied to, and find that, among the families examined, none yields a compact trapdoor. Over Reed--Solomon and algebraic-geometry codes the mask hides a \emph{curve}, and curves are not hidden from jets. 2026/2709.title: Private Accounts Without $O(N)$ Work Through a Hybrid State Model
2026/2709.abstract: Privacy-preserving smart contracts face a scalability problem. In account-balance-vector designs, hiding which accounts changed requires that every transaction perform an indistinguishable update over the global state, so validators pay work linear in the number of accounts for every private transfer. UTXO systems avoid this by validating local spends, but do not provide the same account-style programming model. 2026/2708.title: Beyond Standard Indifferentiability: Simulator Properties for Fiat-Shamir Security
2026/2708.abstract: The Fiat-Shamir transform converts public-coin interactive arguments into non-interactive arguments (NARGs). Its security is typically analyzed in the random-oracle model, while implementations instantiate the random oracle with structured hash constructions. Standard indifferentiability is the natural abstraction for justifying this replacement. Chiesa and Orru (TCC ’25), however, showed that standard indifferentiability does not generally preserve the information and reset behavior needed by common Fiat-Shamir extraction arguments, and proposed stronger notions of indifferentiability to brid

2026/2707.title: Poly Versus Polyval
2026/2707.abstract: We revisit the basic construction of polynomial evaluation based hash function, which we call Poly, over binary extension fields $GF(2^n)$, where $n=64k$ and $k\geq 2$. Unlike GHASH, the NIST standard polynomial evaluation based hash function for $n=128$, Poly does not perform the unnecessary bit reversals of each $n$-bit block, and consequently is faster than GHASH. Further, Poly differs from Polyval, -- a faster alternative to GHASH, -- in that Poly performs usual reduction, while Polyval performs Montgomery reduction. 2026/2706.title: Anamorphic Proofs of Knowledge from Prover Randomness
2026/2706.abstract: Anamorphic encryption and signatures deliver a hidden message through a normal-looking ciphertext or signature. We move from hidden messages to hidden knowledge claims and introduce anamorphic proofs of knowledge, in which a single proof certifies its normal statement publicly while convincing a designated checker that the prover knows a witness for a separately registered anamorphic statement, such as a long-term credential. Our construction reuses a commitment the normal prover already makes to its own randomness. The prover adds a secret mask to the anamorphic witness and uses the sum as th

2026/2705.title: SpreadMAYO: Unlocking Greater Parallelism for Faster MAYO Signatures on GPUs
2026/2705.abstract: Quantum computing threatens public-key cryptography, motivating post-quantum signature standardization. MAYO, a multivariate Round 3 candidate in NIST's additional signature process, offers compact keys and signatures. However, prior GPU implementations do not fully exploit parallelism within each MAYO operation: equation-slice partitioning serializes independent matrix work, while signing requires frequent synchronization among threads during linear-system construction and elimination. We present SpreadMAYO, a high-throughput GPU implementation of MAYO Round 3 that exposes greater parallelism

2026/2704.title: Card-Based Protocols with Mixed Encoding: Computable Functions and the Minimum Number of Cards
2026/2704.abstract: Card-based cryptography performs secure computation with physical cards, where a bit is usually encoded by two cards but can also be encoded by a single card. We study mixed encoding, in which one player gives a single-card commitment and the other a two-card commitment, for perfectly secure protocols with finite runtime and public actions. Mizuki (Theoretical Computer Science, vol.~622, 2016) proposed an AND protocol with mixed encoding as a building block for the conjunction of many variables. 2026/2703.title: Efficient Scalable Oversight via Rewinding
2026/2703.abstract: Scalable oversight asks how a weak verifier can check the outputs of computations performed by more powerful AI systems. One proposed approach uses relativizing interactive proofs, in which a weak verifier checks the output of a complex oracle-aided computation by interacting with one or more powerful provers. A prominent example is debate, which is highly efficient but assumes that one of two powerful AI models, or provers, is truthful. For certain classes of oracle-aided computations, this assumption can be removed, but at substantially greater computational cost. In this work, we introduce

2026/2702.title: The Authentication Complexity of Byzantine Consensus
2026/2702.abstract: Byzantine broadcast and Byzantine agreement are fundamental problems in distributed computing and building blocks for secure multiparty computation. In complete synchronous networks of $n$ parties with channels identifying the immediate sender, classical results establish how authentication changes resilience to $t$ Byzantine faults. Without initially authenticated public keys, both tasks are possible if and only if $n>3t$~\cite{PSL80}. With a complete public-key infrastructure (PKI), broadcast tolerates every $t<n$~\cite{DS83}, and agreement is possible if and only if $n>2t$. These thresholds

2026/2701.title: SPIDER: A Faster and Smaller Identity-Based Signature From Isogenies
2026/2701.abstract: PRISM is an isogeny-based digital signature whose security relies on the problem of computing large prime degree isogenies from a supersingular elliptic curve of unknown endomorphism ring. In this paper, we design SPIDER, a digital signature that builds on a sigma protocol which when given a supersingular elliptic curve $E$, proves the knowledge of an isogeny $\phi: E\rightarrow E'$ of prime (or non smooth) degree $d$. SPIDER can hence be seen as a proof of knowledge of a PRISM signature. The latter observation allows us to combine SPIDER and PRISM to obtain an Identity-Based Signature (IBS) w

2026/2700.title: Practical Collision Attacks on 22- and 23-Step SM3 (Preliminary Version)
2026/2700.abstract: SM3 is a 256-bit cryptographic hash function specified in the Chinese national standard GB/T 32905-2016 and the international standard ISO/IEC 10118-3:2018. In this paper, we present practical collisions for 22- and 23-step SM3 with the standard initial value. Compared with the 20-step collision result of Mendel et al. (2013), our constructions cover two and three additional steps, respectively. The time complexities are approximately \(2^{52.4}\) and \(2^{54.5}\) evaluations of 22- and 23-step SM3, respectively. We also present a semi-free-start collision for 24-step SM3.

2026/2699.title: Registered Functional Encryption with Certified Everlasting Security
2026/2699.abstract: Registered functional encryption removes the trusted authority bottleneck of standard functional encryption by allowing users to register their own public keys, with a transparent aggregation procedure producing a compact master public key. On the other hand, certified everlasting deletion enables a recipient to produce a classical certificate guaranteeing that a ciphertext has been information-theoretically destroyed, even against computationally unbounded adversaries. 2026/2698.title: Batched Identity-Based Encryption with Succinct Publicly Verifiable Subset Deletion
2026/2698.abstract: Batched identity-based encryption (BIBE) compresses a bounded set of identities into a succinct public digest, and provides a single secret key for decrypting ciphertexts associated with identities in the set. We introduce batched identity-based encryption with succinct publicly verifiable subset deletion (BIBE-SPVD), which allows a holder of polynomially many quantum ciphertexts to certify deletion of any chosen subset using a single succinct classical certificate while preserving the usability of the remaining ciphertexts. 2026/2697.title: Batched Threshold Predicate Encryption from Succinct LWE
2026/2697.abstract: Predicate encryption extends attribute-based encryption by providing fine-grained access control while hiding the attribute associated with a ciphertext beyond what the secret keys held by an adversary necessarily reveal. Batched identity-based encryption enables authorization with respect to a designated collection of identities. We introduce batched threshold predicate encryption (BT-PE), which combines batch-scoped authorization, expressive predicate-based access control, and threshold decryption. We give a lattice-based construction supporting polynomial-size arithmetic-circuit predicates,

2026/2696.title: Ratio-Based Ring Oscillator PUF Statistical Model
2026/2696.abstract: A ratio-based ring oscillator physical unclonable function (ROPUF) provides high reliability and is capable of extracting multiple bits from a single ring oscillator pair. However, the derivation of the response bits from such PUFs and the assessment of their randomness have relied only on empirical statistical tests. This paper introduces a novel, mathematically derived closed-form statistical model that characterizes the counter value distribution of the ratio-based ROPUF and formally describes the behavior of this PUF design. 2026/2695.title: Short Collisions Separate Sponge from Merkle-Damgård
2026/2695.abstract: We study short collisions in salted Merkle-Damg{\aa}rd (MD) and Sponge under the query-bounded preprocessing model introduced by Ghoshal and Tessaro (CRYPTO '23). The adversary makes at most $T_1$ oracle queries before a random salt is revealed and at most $T_2$ queries afterwards, and must output two colliding messages of at most $B$ blocks. Our main result is a separation between the two constructions. Let $N=2^n$, give MD and Sponge matching $n$-bit salts, message blocks, and outputs, and set $T_1=\Theta(N/T_2)$ with $T_2=o(\sqrt N)$. 2026/2694.title: Quantum Time-Space Tradeoffs for Short Merkle-Damgård Collisions
2026/2694.abstract: We study time-space tradeoffs for finding short collisions in Merkle-Damg{\aa}rd~(MD) hashing in the quantum auxiliary-input quantum random-oracle model~(QAI-QROM). An adversary may preprocess the compression function into $S$ qubits of arbitrary oracle-dependent quantum advice and, after receiving a fresh salt, make $T$ superposition queries to find a collision consisting of at most $B$ blocks. Previous quantum analyses gave an $\widetilde{O}(ST^3/N)$ security bound for MD collisions with classical advice. 2026/2693.title: Rotom: A Microcontroller-Oriented Tweakable Block Cipher Using Modular Multiplication (Full Version)
2026/2693.abstract: We propose Rotom, a family of 128-bit tweakable block ciphers designed for efficient software implementation on 32-bit microcontrollers. The central design idea is to use modular multiplication as a compact and software-efficient source of strong nonlinearity. Rotom instantiates this idea with a fixed 16-bit S-box built from odd constant multiplication modulo $2^{16}$ interleaved with lightweight linear maps, and combines it with a software-friendly recursive linear layer over four 32-bit words, a compact tweakey schedule, and modular-addition boundary key mixing. 2026/2692.title: Efficient Implementations of Small-Modulus Lattice KEM Components
2026/2692.abstract: Small moduli support compact polynomial representations in lattice-based key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs), including BAT (TCHES 2022) and END (ASIACRYPT 2026, to appear). However, compact encodings can be costly to convert, and uniform generation must account for both coefficient-extraction cost and random-bit demand. Incomplete number-theoretic transforms also leave residual polynomial products. 2026/2691.title: Revisiting Hash-ECB-Hash Enciphering: Plaintext Recovery Attacks on PEP and TET
2026/2691.abstract: Storage encryption motivates tweakable enciphering schemes, which encrypt entire multi-block data units without length expansion and use a public tweak to identify their context. We revisit PEP (FSE 2006) and TET (CRYPTO 2007), two Hash-ECB-Hash schemes that combine parallel block-cipher calls with invertible mixing, and present classical distinguishing and plaintext-recovery attacks. For PEP, we exhibit a fixed public field satisfying the published parameter-selection rule whose generated position coefficients repeat. 2026/2690.title: Gaussian Difference Dynamics: Breaking the $2^{n/2}$ Barrier for the Shortest Vector Problem and Discrete Gaussian Sampling
2026/2690.abstract: We give classical randomized algorithms in a word-RAM model that break the $2^{n/2}$ barrier for both discrete Gaussian sampling (DGS) and the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP). For every fixed $\alpha>1$, shifted DGS on arbitrary lattices at width $\sigma\ge\alpha\eta_{1/2}(L)$ takes $$ (3/2)^{n/2+o(n)}\text{ time} \qquad\text{and}\qquad (4/3)^{n/2+o(n)}\text{ space}. $$ These bounds match the Becker--Ducas--Gama--Laarhoven (BDGL) heuristic sieving exponents. 2026/2689.title: Weir: Bounded-Memory Indexing and Proving with Sequential Storage
2026/2689.abstract: A low-memory prover must control sumcheck tables, sparse accesses, commitments and proof assembly. We present Weir, a Shockwave-derived protocol with a complete read-write (RW) index-and-prove schedule. The schedule restores sparse request order, retains commitment state through later openings and assembles the proof externally. These steps preserve the direct RAM prover's canonical bytes across buffer choices, with a common verifier. 2026/2688.title: Elliptic Curve Arithmetic for Quantum Cryptanalysis: A Study of Curve25519
2026/2688.abstract: Recent quantum resource estimates over prime fields have largely focused on prime order elliptic curves. We implement modern affine circuit techniques on the widely deployed composite order curve, Curve25519, and obtain a scalar circuit using 47,199,530 CCX gates and 1,189 peak logical qubits. This uses approximately 35% and 18% fewer gates than Schrottenloher's published space- and gate-optimized secp256k1 circuits, respectively. We separate three contributions. First, we apply established arithmetic and signed table techniques to Curve25519. In a comparison using the same arithmetic framewor

2026/2687.title: Penalty Deposits For Discrete Logarithms
2026/2687.abstract: We propose a technique that allows a trusted party in some protocol to attach deposits to their own secrets, without impacting security, and convincing other parties using zero-knowledge proofs. The rationale is that, should this party compromise the protocol by blundering or revealing its secrets, they lose the attached deposit to attackers. As a result, stakeholders gain confidence on how this trusted party operates, and breaches become public as soon as deposits are claimed. 2026/2686.title: Provable Recovery from Integer Quotients: Improved Bounds for Nonlinear Hidden Number Problems
2026/2686.abstract: The hidden number problem (HNP) asks whether a secret can be recovered from partial information about values linked to it by known algebraic relations. In cryptosystems where partial information about secret values or internal randomness is leaked across various scenarios, HNP techniques provide a foundational framework for security analysis and key-recovery attacks. For some HNPs with nonlinear relations, provable polynomial-time recovery guarantees have long remained unimproved, requiring a substantial fraction of the leading bits. 2026/2685.title: Quasi-polynomial time algorithms for block basis reduction of linear codes
2026/2685.abstract: The block code basis reduction algorithm (BKZ) proposed by Ghentiyala and Stephens-Davidowitz requires an exponential number of calls to the minimum weight codeword (MWC) oracle according to the weak complexity bounds established in the original paper. In almost all cases these bounds are worse than plain enumeration of codewords, despite the fact that in practice the algorithm works much better. In this work we propose block code basis reduction algorithms with polynomial and quasi-polynomial complexity for fixed $\beta$. Our algorithms are relaxations and modifications of the original algori

2026/2684.title: SoK: Multiple Concurrent Proposer Blockchains
2026/2684.abstract: Multiple concurrent proposer (MCP) protocols let several parties contribute transactions to the same ledger update. They can distribute communication and reduce one proposer's control over inclusion and order, but these benefits depend on how the contributions are combined. We describe a common architecture from transaction receipt through proposal formation, agreement, data recovery, ordering, execution, and state finality. Within it, we identify four direct MCP families: fixed proposal vectors, selected proposal collections, persistent proposal streams, and causal proposal DAGs. We compare t

2026/2683.title: Stop Calling Them Provers: The Case for Calling ProVerif and Tamarin Symbolic Protocol Analyzers
2026/2683.abstract: A claim that a cryptographic protocol has been proved secure depends on the theory, the analysis software, the protocol model, and the security property being checked. I examine each of these for ProVerif and Tamarin. An audit of their published soundness arguments finds false statements, missing proofs, and gaps between the procedures justified on paper and those the tools run. I also reproduce previously reported bugs that cause Tamarin to accept false claims about the submitted models. ProVerif supplies no certificate for its full analysis, while Tamarin replays its proof tree with its own

2026/2682.title: A Quantitative Evaluation of Constant-Time Analysis Tools
2026/2682.abstract: The constant-time programming policy protects cryptographic code from timing side-channels. However, writing constant-time code remains challenging even for experienced developers. Therefore, over 50 CT analysis tools have been published to help them identify constant-time violations. While several studies have examined those tools, they predominantly rely on qualitative observations and case studies, rather than quantitative assessments. Therefore, we present AutoBench-CT, a modular benchmark that manually verified per-violation ground truths across 64 cryptographic tasks and the first unifie

2026/2681.title: Improving Code Rate and Query Complexity for the Ligero-IOP System
2026/2681.abstract: This work presents two main contributions to the analysis and design of Ligero-style zero-knowledge proof systems. First, we analyze the original Ligero IOP in the list-decoding regime and show that mutual correlated agreement suffices to obtain improved soundness guarantees and lower query complexity, without modifying the protocol. Second, we propose a new variant of Ligero that incorporates out-of-domain sampling, leading to further soundness improvements and enabling Reed--Solomon code rates above $1/2$. The new protocol preserves the constant-round structure of the Ligero IOP and its comp

2026/2680.title: (Balanced) Boolean Functions on 375 Variables with Nonlinearity Exceeding the Patterson-Wiedemann Direct-Sum Bound
2026/2680.abstract: Patterson and Wiedemann [IEEE-IT 1983] constructed Boolean functions on 15 variables with nonlinearity 16276, which is strictly greater than the bent concatenation bound. Taking their direct sum with a bent function gives nonlinearity $2^{n-1}-27\cdot2^{(n-11)/2}$ for every odd $n\ge15$. Much later, Schmidt [JCT-A 2019] proved that the asymptotic maximum nonlinearity is $2^{n-1}-(1+o(1))2^{n/2-1}$ as $n\to\infty$. 2026/2679.title: Cryptanalysis and Enhancement of VTBSAE: Provably Secure Verifier-Based PAKE Protocols for the Industrial Internet of Things
2026/2679.abstract: Verifier‑based password‑authenticated key exchange (PAKE) enables a client and a server to establish high‑entropy session keys from low‑entropy passwords without requiring the server to store plaintext passwords. This asymmetric design reduces the risk that leakage of server‑side credentials directly leads to client impersonation, making verifier‑based PAKE well suited to authentication and session‑key establishment for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices. 2026/2678.title: From Quantum Mechanics to the Hidden Subgroup Problem: an Overview from Finite to Infinite Groups
2026/2678.abstract: The Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP for short) is an important problem in quantum computing and computational group theory, which has connections with several quantum algorithms, including Shor's algorithm for integer factorization and the discrete logarithm problem. The HSP can be stated as follows: given a function on a group that is constant and distinct on cosets of a hidden subgroup, determine the hidden subgroup efficiently. The problem captures the essence of exploiting group structures for computational advantage and provides insights into the power of quantum algorithms over classical ap

2026/2677.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugatess
2026/2677.abstract: Let \(E\) be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over \(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p\) and \(\delta_E\) be the minimum degree of isogenies from \(E\) to its Frobenius conjugate \(E^{(p)}\). We establish bounds for the smoothness probability of $\delta_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's \(p^{1/3+o(1)}\) attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional. 2026/2676.title: Optimality and Efficiency of Higher-Order Rank-Based Side-Channel Attacks against Inner Product Masking Schemes
2026/2676.abstract: Higher-Order Spearman Coefficient Analysis (HO-SPA) is of particular interest in non-profiling Side-Channel Attacks (SCA) due to its effectiveness against monotonic nonlinear leakage. However, the optimal form, effective order combinations, and performance of HO-SPA (or its variants) remain underexplored. This work systematically revisits HO-SPA in the presence of Boolean Masking (BM) and Inner Product Masking (IPM). Specifically, we propose a new variant of HO-SPA, called HO-ASPA (Higher-Order Adjusted Spearman Coefficient Analysis), and derive the optimal form of HO-ASPA for two-share BM and

2026/2675.title: High Precision Noise Cleaning for CKKS with Application to Asynchronous Threshold CKKS
2026/2675.abstract: Noise cleaning in discrete CKKS uses Hermite interpolation to reduce the input error while preserving the encrypted discrete message. Cryptographic applications based on noise flooding require the error after cleaning to be sufficiently small for the added noise to provide statistical hiding without preventing exact recovery. This requirement is more stringent than decryption correctness alone, but the achievable noise reduction is limited by errors introduced during homomorphic evaluation. 2026/2674.title: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design
2026/2674.abstract: The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings. Adaptive clinching enjoys compelling guarantees: it is Pareto optimal, and truthful bidding is a dominant strategy whenever budgets cannot be overreported. In many real-world environments, however, identities are cheap to create, making resilience to Sybil attacks an additional requirement. Whether the guarantees of adaptive clinching survive when a bidder can s

2026/2673.title: Beyond the Scope of This Paper: Practical Flash-Accelerator and Cache-Collision Timing Attacks on Microcontrollers
2026/2673.abstract: Cache and cache-collision attacks against AES are well-known since 2005, but their application to small (Cortex-M sized) microcontrollers has been limited in prior work, and in many cases the devices are assumed to be immune when they do not have a cache. However, the flash architecture of almost all microcontrollers introduces the same timing collision required for the well-known attacks and as a greatly underestimated channel. Recovery of AES keys using as little as 750 traces will be demonstrated on six popular cryptographic libraries across eight architectures and over twenty devices. Prac

2026/2672.title: Nenya: Efficient zkSNARKs for Integer Rings Z/2kZ via Reverse Multiplication-Friendly Embeddings
2026/2672.abstract: Zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (zkSNARKs) are powerful cryptographic tools for certifying the correctness of computations with short proofs, fast verification, and zero-knowledge privacy guarantees. However, most existing zkSNARK schemes support arithmetic only over finite fields defined by large primes or their extensions. This creates substantial overhead when proving computations written in high-level programming languages, which typically operate on fixed-width integer types such as 32-bit and 64-bit integers. In this paper, we introduce Nenya, the first pra

2026/2671.title: Beyond the Event Horizon of Keccak, Extending the Observation from 2011 and applications
2026/2671.abstract: In 2011 we observed that a single path in the Keccak sponge from a state whose capacity has all zero bits back to such a state yields an explicit, infinite family of second preimages for every message of at least one full rate block. Finding such a path costs about 2^(c/2), which lies "beyond the event horizon" for SHA3-256 (c = 512). In this paper we give four novel theorems around that observation. 2026/2670.title: Barriers to Identity-Based Encryption in Generic Group-Action Models
2026/2670.abstract: Identity-based encryption (IBE) is required to support a superpolynomial-size identity space using only polynomial-size public parameters. This compression requirement underlies known barriers to IBE in the generic (pairing-free) group model. Cryptographic group actions, motivated prominently by isogeny-based cryptography, support many advanced primitives beyond public-key encryption. However, no generic construction of IBE from the basic group-action interface is known. 2026/2669.title: PIR through the Lens of Probabilistic Inference
2026/2669.abstract: Private Information Retrieval (PIR) allows a client to retrieve an entry of a database while revealing no information about the requested index to the servers. Classic information-theoretic PIR protocols of Chor et al. (FOCS '95, JACM '98) and Ambainis (ICALP '97) achieve sublinear client computation and communication complexity with a constant number of servers, but require each server to perform computation linear in the database size. 2026/2668.title: An Algebraic Polynomial Evaluation Datastructure for Fields of Large Characteristic
2026/2668.abstract: In this work, we study (multivariate) polynomial evaluation datastructures, i.e. algorithms that can evaluate a multivariate polynomial at any input point, using random access to some precomputed encoding of the polynomial. Multiple constructions have been proposed in the literature, with the work by Bhargava, Ghosh, Guo, Kumar and Umans (2024) achieving optimal datastructure size and query complexity, up to polynomial factors. 2026/2667.title: Faster complete formulas and their application to curves with efficient endomorphisms
2026/2667.abstract: We revisit scalar multiplication on prime curves $y^2 = x^3 + b$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, a family that includes secp256k1, BN and BLS curves. Applying a 15-year-old technique in a new way, we improve the best complete addition from $12$ to $11$ multiplications ($10$ in mixed coordinates), the first improvement in 10 years: its final stage is a 3D cross product, which needs only five multiplications. 2026/2666.title: Efficient SIMD SHAKE through Cost-Aware Permutation Scheduling
2026/2666.abstract: Lattice-based cryptography uses SHAKE to expand seeds into byte strings for matrix generation and sampling. SIMD Keccak implementations process multiple hash streams in parallel. Differences in stream lengths and input dependencies can prevent full SIMD utilization. We present a cost-aware method for scheduling Keccak permutations across hash streams during a single execution of a cryptographic algorithm. 2026/2665.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days
2026/2665.abstract: We present an end-to-end resource estimation of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, from its mathematical description to the allocation and scheduling of physical qubits on a chip layout. After proposing a comprehensive view of the modern versions of Shor's algorithm for RSA, ECDLP and FFDLP, we make explicit their logical circuits and the trade-offs they enable. We compile the dominant subroutines down to physical-qubit operations on two architectures: one based on repetition cat codes and one based on LDPC cat codes. 2026/2664.title: Rerandomizable Garbling Beyond BHHO-KMHE and a Construction from LWE
2026/2664.abstract: Rerandomizable garbling schemes (RGS) are a fundamental primitive enabling advanced cryptographic constructions such as multi-hop homomorphic encryption (Gentry, Halevi, Vaikuntanathan, CRYPTO 2010), iO-combiners (Ananth, Jain, Naor, Sahai, Yogev, CRYPTO 2016), and YOSO-style MPC (Acharya, Hazay, Kolesnikov, Prabhakaran, TCC 2022 and CRYPTO 2024). All known RGS instantiations rely on discrete-logarithm-type assumptions, concretely via the BHHO scheme (Boneh, Halevi, Hamburg, Ostrovsky, CRYPTO 2008) and its recent pairing-based variant (Heitjohann, von der Heyden, Jager, CRYPTO 2025). 2026/2663.title: Quantum Multi-Collision Lower Bounds for Arbitrary Bounded Types
2026/2663.abstract: We study quantum collision finding for functions of prescribed exact type. For fixed constants $k\ge r\ge2$ and $N=kn$, consider functions $f:[N]\to\mathbb Z_q$ of type $(k^n)$, with exactly $n$ distinct output values and $k$ preimages for each value. We prove that the worst-case bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding $r$-collisions in $\ell$ distinct equality classes is \[ \Theta_{k,r}\!\left( \ell^{\,2^{r-1}/(2^r-1)} N^{(2^{r-1}-1)/(2^r-1)} \right) \] for $1\le\ell\le N^{2^{-r}}$. 2026/2662.title: Tractable, Not Truncated: Colored-Noise TRNG Security via Fractional Brownian Motion
2026/2662.abstract: Oscillator-based true random number generators derive randomness from timing fluctuations driven by thermal and flicker noise, and flicker gains weight as technology advances and transistors shrink. Its long memory leaks information about past, which existing models either discard or truncate, overstating security. We introduce a rigorous and tractable framework for colored noise, including the white and flicker noise of oscillators. 2026/2661.title: Radical isogenies on every model
2026/2661.abstract: Radical isogeny formulae compute a cyclic chain of $N$-isogenies with one $N$th root per step and without sampling torsion points, but for general $N$ they were only known in Tate normal form. We give radical steps of every odd degree $N$ directly on short Weierstrass, Montgomery, twisted Edwards, Huff, extended Jacobi quartic, twisted Hessian, Legendre and Jacobi intersection curves, on Kummer lines, and on all curves with a rational point of order~$2$. 2026/2660.title: Towards Quantum Sensing for Side-Channel Analysis
2026/2660.abstract: Side-Channel Analysis is an established field of research to assess implementation vulnerabilities of cryptographic algorithms. One typically exploited side-channel is the electromagnetic (EM) near-field, which is proportional to the data-dependent currents flowing through an Integrated Circuit (IC). The field of Quantum Sensing (QS) based on Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers has shown promising approaches for different measurement configurations like scanning or spatially resolved wide-field imaging. 2026/2659.title: Alg\{Ossa\}: Decentralized Secure Aggregation with Rotating Committees and Eventual Delivery
2026/2659.abstract: Secure aggregation lets clients reveal only an aggregate of their private contributions, supporting a variety of applications, including privacy-preserving sensing, collaborative analytics, and federated learning. Building on the single-server, committee-aided model for one-shot clients used by OPA and Willow~(CRYPTO~'25), we present Ossa, a generic construction with a modular security analysis. 2026/2658.title: Unshuffling Fisher-Yates: Practical Recovery of Length-128 Permutations and Application to ML-DSA
2026/2658.abstract: Shuffling is a standard hiding countermeasure against (single-trace) side-channel attacks on the number-theoretic transform (NTT) of lattice-based post-quantum schemes, such as ML-DSA. The Fisher-Yates algorithm can be used to generate the underlying random permutation. Recovering this permutation itself from a single trace has so far only been studied for short sequences. We present a practical attack on a software implementation of Fisher-Yates for sequences of length 128, the number of butterfly operations in one layer of ML-DSA’s NTT. 2026/2657.title: Poly2MsgLeaks: Certified Key Recovery from Polynomial-to-Message Leakage
2026/2657.abstract: We present Poly2MsgLeaks, a profiled chosen-ciphertext power-analysis attack that recovers the complete 512-coefficient public-key encryption (PKE) secret of SMAUG-T in its TiMER parameter set. Each polynomial-to-message (P2M) decision depends on four ternary secret coefficients and therefore on one of 81 local states. We characterize all admissible P2M predicates and show that our six-query schedule maps the 81 states to 57 binary transcripts; even with both exact polynomial weights, noiseless transcripts leave a mean residual ambiguity of 27.2 bits. 2026/2656.title: Falcon Key Recovery from Joint Sampler Leakages
2026/2656.abstract: Falcon and the forthcoming FN-DSA standard based on it generate signatures via discrete Gaussian sampling, during which power consumption leaks information about secret-dependent intermediate values. While prior attacks exploit sampler leakages individually or in pairs, we present a unified key-recovery framework that fuses three observations from each SamplerZ call: the signed-exponent class e(k) of the integer center, the random-sign bit b, and a multi-class proposal magnitude z0. 2026/2655.title: OblivDGL: Oblivious Deep Graph Learning Made Practical
2026/2655.abstract: The rapid deployment of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) within Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) has opened up new privacy concerns. Both sensitive graph data and proprietary GNN models are submitted to and processed in third-party MLaaS platform for training and inference. To alleviate those concerns, recent efforts have been made to design tailored secure computation protocols for GNNs. Unfortunately, existing designs cannot accomplish security, functionality, and scalability simultaneously. 2026/2654.title: When Algebraic Structure Meets Too Many Hints
2026/2654.abstract: The hint framework of Dachman-Soled, Ducas, Gong, and Rossi (CRYPTO 2020), together with the later too-many-hints analyses from May and Nowakowski (ASIACRYPT 2023) and Cao, Jiang, and Cheng (CRYPTO 2025), gives a classification of secret-dependent hints and LLL-breaking hint thresholds for LWE schemes. These values are now frequently adopted as the default benchmark for side-channel security evaluation. We show that applying them as a security metric is problematic. 2026/2653.title: Analyzing Compiler-induced Constant-time Violations with Compiler at Scale
2026/2653.abstract: The constant-time programming policy is a de facto standard for cryptographic libraries to prevent timing side-channel attacks. However, compiler optimizations may break constant-time source code during compilation. Systematically preventing this requires understanding where a violation arises, how it is introduced, and which compiler configurations are problematic. 2026/2652.title: Reverse Substitution in Secret Sharing: The Critical One-Half Threshold and a Route to Superpolynomial Lower Bounds
2026/2652.abstract: The contribution vector (convec) of a secret-sharing scheme is the vector of its normalized share sizes. The average and maximum coordinates of a convec give, respectively, the average and maximum information ratios of the scheme. Obtaining superlinear lower bounds on these quantities for unrestricted perfect secret sharing has remained a challenging open problem for about four decades. 2026/2651.title: HELLO, GOODBYE: Concurrent General Composition From Super-Rushing Security
2026/2651.abstract: Kushilevitz, Lindell, and Rabin (STOC `06, SIAM Journal on Computing `10), in their seminal result, showed that any standalone-secure synchronous multiparty computation (MPC) protocol can be compiled into one secure under concurrent general composition, by adding a synchronisation step after every round; thereby, at least doubling the round complexity. We show that for protocols that are secure against super-rushing adversaries, introduced by Asharov, Chandramouli, Cohen, and Ishai (EuroCrypt `25), two synchronisation rounds suffice. 2026/2650.title: On Robust Combiners for Pseudorandom Codes and PKE with Pseudorandom Ciphertexts
2026/2650.abstract: Robust combiners are a standard way to hedge cryptographic assumptions: given several candidate constructions, they produce one construction that remains secure as long as one candidate is secure. In favorable cases, such combiners also yield universal constructions. We ask whether this paradigm applies to cryptographic primitives whose public outputs must be both pseudorandom and sparse. 2026/2649.title: LINE-Break: Cryptanalysis and Reverse Engineering of Letter Sealing
2026/2649.abstract: We present a security analysis of the messaging service known as LINE, a popular platform used daily by millions of users in East and Southeast Asia – most notably Japan, Taiwan, Thailand, and Indonesia. More specifically, we focus on its underlying custom end-to-end encryption (E2EE) protocol, known as Letter Sealing v2. Our findings show that Letter Sealing allows a TLS Machine-in-the- Middle attacker or malicious server to violate integrity, authenticity, and confidentiality of communications. 2026/2648.title: Notes on BulletProofs++ Range Proofs
2026/2648.abstract: We review the Bulletproofs++ construction which replaces the bit-decomposition inner-product argument of Bulletproofs with a reciprocal set-membership argument over base-$16$ digits. We present a self-contained specification of the $64$-bit range proof as well as a general batched variant parametric in the batch size $M$ and bit width $b$ and prove honest-verifier zero-knowledge and exact-form knowledge soundness. 2026/2647.title: Revisiting ZMAC+: Birthday-Bound Attacks and a Beyond-Birthday-Bound Repair
2026/2647.abstract: ZMAC+ is a tweakable-block-cipher-based MAC proposed by List and Nandi in ToSC 2017 with claimed beyond-birthday-bound security. We show that a tag-swap mechanism previously observed for a hypothetical two-output extension of DoveMAC also applies to the published ZMAC+ construction. For two-block tags, we give a distinguisher with constant advantage and a fresh-message forgery with constant success probability using $O(2^{n/2})$ queries in the ideal-TBC model, where $n$ is the block length. 2026/2646.title: Mikros: Bitwidth-Aware SNARKs over Extensions of Small Fields
2026/2646.abstract: Provers for succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs) perform arithmetic over a large field for soundness, even when the witness entries are a few bits wide, which inflates both prover time and memory usage. Recent work makes individual SNARK components bitwidth-aware, so that a lower witness bitwidth means faster proving and lower memory usage, but these techniques cover only part of the prover and exploit the structure of specific fields, typically binary ones. We introduce Mikros, a framework for end-to-end bitwidth-aware SNARK construction based on algebraic vector packing.

2026/2645.title: Isotaxis: Optimal Asynchronous Byzantine Consensus with Ordering Linearizability
2026/2645.abstract: Despite ensuring both consistency and liveness, state machine replication (SMR) protocols remain vulnerable to adversaries that manipulate transaction order, causing, e.g., MEV attacks. To mitigate this, researchers have proposed new variants augmented with order-fairness. However, existing protocols that employ dependency graphs, such as Aequitas (Crypto 2020), Themis (CCS 2023), and SpeedyFair (NDSS 2024), often suffer from suboptimal performance, limited resilience, or weakened security guarantees. 2026/2644.title: Iterated-Logarithmic Additive Hardness for Bin Packing
2026/2644.abstract: The question of obtaining a constant-additive approximation for bin packing was highlighted in the third of ten open problems in Williamson and Shmoys' The Design of Approximation Algorithms [SW11, Chapter~17, Problem~3]. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$, no deterministic polynomial-time packing using at most $\mathrm{OPT}+c\log^*\mathrm{OPT}$ bins, where $\mathrm{OPT}$ is the minimum number of bins. 2026/2643.title: Non-profiled Single-Trace ML-DSA Secret Key Recovery by Horizontal Distribution Analysis
2026/2643.abstract: During the last decade, single-trace side-channel attacks on cryptographic implementations have largely focused on profiled methods, which typically assume that the attacker has a clone device and implementation knowledge to build a leakage model for the target before launching the attack. In this paper, we demonstrate that a much weaker adversary, without the ability to profile, can also mount powerful single-trace attacks. 2026/2642.title: Cryptanalysis and Repair of "Decentralized Multi-authority ABE for NC$^1$ from BDH"
2026/2642.abstract: We present a plaintext-recovery attack on both the DBDH-based construction and the CBDH-based variant of Datta, Komargodski, and Waters (Journal of Cryptology, 2023). The attack succeeds with probability one in the claimed static security model using one corrupt authority and two users, each unauthorized even when granted the corrupt authority's attribute. 2026/2641.title: A Memory-efficient Implementation of Wiedemann XL
2026/2641.abstract: The signature schemes MQOM, SNOVA, MAYO, and UOV are third-round candidates in the NIST standardization process for additional post-quantum signatures, and their security relies on the hardness of the multivariate quadratic (MQ) problem. XL with block Wiedemann (BW) is one of the most efficient MQ solvers in practice, but its memory demand has led to a debate about its memory access cost: generating the rows of the Macaulay matrix on the fly is widely believed to save memory at a non-negligible computational cost. 2026/2640.title: Subexponential Algorithms for LWE via Rejection Sampling on Superlattices
2026/2640.abstract: Recent superlattice algorithms have improved the provable complexity of lattice problems. Ducas, Engelberts, and Loyer used this framework to obtain a subexponential algorithm for infinity-norm short integer solution, while also identifying a key obstacle to extending it to learning with errors (LWE). A similar difficulty arose in the analysis of Kirchner and Fouque, whose claimed subexponential running time with only linearly many LWE samples was not rigorously established. 2026/2639.title: Private Information Retrieval with Accountability at Erasure-Optimal Server Redundancy
2026/2639.abstract: Private information retrieval (PIR) hides which database item a client requests. We study PIR that also identifies servers that respond incorrectly. Against a coalition of at most $t$ corrupted servers, the client must retrieve the item and identify every deviating server when at most $d$ deviate. 2026/2638.title: Decision Attacks on Known-Covariance Ring-LWE via Public Gram Determinants
2026/2638.abstract: Known-Covariance Ring-LWE (KCov-RLWE) was introduced by Micciancio and Suhl to support simulation-secure threshold encryption. It strengthens ordinary Ring-LWE by revealing an exact quadratic summary of the hidden secret and errors, and its decisional hardness was left open. We give explicit polynomial-time decision attacks for broad families of prime moduli at ring rank one. 2026/2637.title: Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Gabidulin Codes Is NP-Hard Even in Dimension One
2026/2637.abstract: Fix a prime power q . We prove that deciding whether a received word y ∈ F^n_qm lies at rank distance at most n − 2 from the one-dimensional Gabidulin code {λg : λ in Fqm } is NP-complete. Thus maximum-likelihood decoding of Gabidulin codes is NP-hard even for k = 1, an analogue of the Guruswami-Vardy theorem for Reed-Solomon codes. In the Hamming metric, by contrast, hardness at this radius requires the dimension to grow with the length, as in the Guruswami Vardy theorem. 2026/2636.title: Revisiting AES Key Wrap: Forgery Bounds, Structural Observations, and Recommendations for the Revision of NIST SP 800-38F
2026/2636.abstract: NIST is revising SP~800-38F, which specifies the AES Key Wrap modes KW and KWP. This paper is an updated and expanded version of our technical comments to NIST. We show that the forgery probabilities stated in SP~800-38F do not account for adaptive attacks, give the resulting forgery probabilities for KW, KWP, and TKW, and show that checking the expected plaintext length can raise the security level of KWP considerably. Revisiting Kelsey's long-message observation, we correct the collision conditions, show that a successful forgery leaks a plaintext prefix, derive an encryption-only distinguis

2026/2635.title: A Kelsey–Kohno Attack Variant against SHA-2 Message Digests in HSS/LMS and XMSS
2026/2635.abstract: We present a multi-target second-preimage attack on the message hashing of the stateful hash-based signature schemes HSS/LMS and XMSS with SHA-256 and with the truncated SHA-256/192. The attack builds on the herding technique of Kelsey and Kohno: the attacker takes the chaining states that follow the per-signature prefixes of many collected signatures and merges them, level by level through state collisions, into a single chaining state. From that state one search serves all collected signatures at once, which defeats the commitment to the key and to the one-time-signature leaf index at the st

2026/2634.title: Nearly Optimal Hardness for CVP and NCP with Preprocessing
2026/2634.abstract: The closest vector problem(CVP)and the nearest codeword problem (NCP) are fundamental computational problems with connections to learning, coding theory, and cryptography. We study hardness of approximation in the preprocessing model: an algorithm receives the lattice or code in advance, may perform unrestricted computation to produce polynomial-size advice, and must then solve the problem on any target in polynomial time. Unless $\mathsf{NP} \subseteq \mathsf{P/poly}$, no such algorithm achieves an approximation factor of $\bullet$ $M^{1−\varepsilon}$ for NCP over any fixed finite field, or $

2026/2633.title: On the Inapplicability of Residue-Confined Error Attacks to CRT-FHE with Non-Degenerate Error Distributions
2026/2633.abstract: This paper responds to the cryptanalysis presented in “Key Recovery from Residue- Confined Errors in the Pradhan CRT-RLWE Construction” (Olejnik and Naskrecki, 2026), which claims key recovery and plaintext recovery against the CRT-FHE scheme introduced in “A New CRT-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption” (Pradhan et al., 2026). We demonstrate that the reported recovery attacks rely entirely on a deliberately con- structed error distribution whose support lies in the kernel of the CRT encoding function. Consequently, the effective encryption error is identically zero, reducing the attacked con- s

2026/2632.title: Chosen Commitments and Certified Decoding Regions in the Adaptive Threshold Schnorr Attack
2026/2632.abstract: Crites and Stewart reduce an adaptive forgery attack on threshold Schnorr signatures with $N$ parties and threshold $\tau$ to one call to a sparse linear search oracle, which they show to be bounded distance decoding of a diagonally scaled Reed–Solomon code and whose sparse answer, a witness, names the parties to corrupt. Their analysis samples the coefficient vector behind the adversary's commitment uniformly at random and leaves open whether a chosen vector does better. 2026/2631.title: On the Subtleties of Non-Malleability in IVC: Notions, Attacks and Constructions from Falsifiable Assumptions
2026/2631.abstract: We investigate non-malleable Incrementally Verifiable Computation (IVC), a subject that has received limited attention. We focus on whether and how simulation-sound IVC can be obtained from falsifiable assumptions. We provide additional evidence of the unique aspects of non-malleable incremental proofs, identifying definitional challenges in formalizing simulation-sound IVC, and showing how existing IVC designs from falsifiable assumptions cannot exhibit simulation-soundness "for free" (without modifications). In addition to a new family of definitions of simulation-sound IVC, our main results

2026/2630.title: Exact Error Bootstrapping and Comb Bootstrapping in FHEW/TFHE
2026/2630.abstract: In FHEW and TFHE, bootstrapping evaluates the decryption function via a blind rotation, whose resolution limits the message space. We propose instead to bootstrap the \emph{error}. By rounding the ciphertext at a resolution that is a multiple of the message modulus, we preserve the message exactly. Reduction modulo a small integer then yields a noise-free encryption of the error, which a single blind rotation lifts exactly before it is subtracted. The message modulus is thus constrained solely by the noise and can be much larger than in standard TFHE. Since the error takes far fewer distinct v

2026/2629.title: VeilDNS: Post-Quantum DNS Privacy from the First UDP Packet
2026/2629.abstract: DNS was designed around UDP, and most DNS traffic today still follows that design: one query, one response, and no handshake. This makes DNS fast and scalable, but exposes client queries in cleartext. DoT, DoH, and DoQ provide privacy by encrypting DNS messages with TLS. This works once TLS/TCP or QUIC handshakes complete, but cold sessions spend extra round trips and CPU before the first private query can be sent—a cost that grows with post-quantum cryptography. 2026/2628.title: Extraction meets Distillation - cryptanalytic techniques to recover parameters from a Deep Neural Network
2026/2628.abstract: We study fully connected neural-network reconstruction by combining cryptanalytic weight-direction extraction with learning from predicted labels. We adapt a ReLU extraction implementation to Leaky ReLU, compare sign-search methods, and estimate biases and output layers. We prove conditional bounds for direction recovery with approximate prefixes, preservation of local distance votes, prediction changes from aligned parameter errors, and sign selection with independent scoring data. 2026/2627.title: Strongly Adaptive Asynchronous Byzantine Agreement with Linear Communication and Almost-Everywhere Termination
2026/2627.abstract: It is well known that Byzantine agreement requires $\Omega(t^2)$ messages against a strongly adaptive adversary that may corrupt $t=\Theta(n)$ parties and suppress a party's undelivered messages upon corruption. We circumvent this lower bound by relaxing termination: for any constant $0<\nu<1$, at least a $(1-\nu)$ fraction of the honest parties terminate, while agreement and validity hold for every honest decision. 2026/2626.title: The Exact Bit Security of Hash-Based Signatures
2026/2626.abstract: In this work, we analyze the security of hash-based signatures in Lean4. We examine how different ways of accounting for an adversary’s work yield different notions of bit security. As our working example, we study two instances of XMSS with $128$ bit digests. Under most of the accounting modes we consider, we get $127$ bit security for strong unforgeability. However, under the most conservative convention that counts only the adversary’s direct random oracle queries, we only get $122$ bits of security. We prove these bounds in the random oracle model without computational hardness assumptions

2026/2625.title: Faster Polynomial Factorization over Finite Fields via Batched Modular Composition
2026/2625.abstract: In the algebraic model, where one counts operations in $\mathbb{F}_q$ uniformly in the characteristic, the best published algorithm for factoring a polynomial of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, due to Kaltofen and Shoup with the rectangular products of Huang and Pan, uses $n^{1.80535+o(1)}\log q$ operations, and its bottleneck is the modular compositions of the giant steps. A new algorithm is presented for these compositions. Like the algorithm of Neiger, Salvy, Schost and Villard, the new method is based on the relation matrices of the argument. 2026/2624.title: Provable Security of SHA-256-Based LMS Revisited in the Ideal-Cipher Model
2026/2624.abstract: The hash-based Leighton-Micali Signature (LMS) has been standardized by IETF, NIST and ISO. State-of-the-art non-quantum security proofs for LMS have been given by Katz (SSR 2016) and Fluhrer (Eprint 2017/553). However, the actual structure of SHA-256(/192) is the (chopped) Merkle-Damg{\aa}rd construction using a blockcipher-based Davies-Meyer function, and precise security bounds of SHA-256-based LMS\_SHA256\_M32 and SHA-256/192-based LMS\_SHA256\_M24 should be derived in the {\it ideal-cipher model (ICM)}. 2026/2623.title: The Covering Radius of $\operatorname{RM}(2,8)$ is Between $88$ and $91$
2026/2623.abstract: Let $\operatorname{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed--Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. The values $\rho(2,6)=18$ and $\rho(2,7)=40$ are known, whereas the exact value of $\rho(2,8)$ remains open. Starting from the current state of the art bound $88\leq\rho(2,8)\leq96$, we give a computer-assisted reduction of the upper bound $\rho(2,8)\leq91$. We first show that every even-weight Boolean function on eight variables is within distance $90$ of a quadratic function. Changing one value then gives the bound $91$ for odd-weight functions. 2026/2622.title: Faster Matrix Multiplication Leads to Faster Lattice Sieving
2026/2622.abstract: Let $\omega$ denote the matrix multiplication exponent. Very recently, OpenAI showed that $\omega\le9/4$. We demonstrate that, for any fixed $\eta>0$, if $\omega\le9/4-\eta$, then there is a constant $\delta=\delta(\eta)>0$ such that heuristic lattice sieving can be improved to $(3/2-\delta)^{n/2+o(n)}$ time under the spherical heuristic used in the BDGL analysis. With known matrix multiplication algorithms, our method already yields subquadratic search within BDGL buckets.

2026/2621.title: Bounds on polynomial approximations of the discrete logarithm function
2026/2621.abstract: We revisit a classical result of Coppersmith and Shparlinski [CS00] showing bounds on how well polynomials can approximate the discrete log function. They showed that for any univariate polynomial $f(X) \in \mathbb{F}_p[X]$ with $\deg(f) \leq D$, we have: $$ |\{ x \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times \mid f(x) = \mathsf{dlog}(x) \}| \leq \sqrt{2 D p}.$$ We show two improvements: (1) For all $D$, we improve the upper bound above to $(1+o(1)) \cdot \sqrt{Dp}$. 2026/2620.title: When Elliptic-Curve Semiprimality Certificates Reveal Factors
2026/2620.abstract: Public certificates of semiprimality could support cryptographic modulus generation by proving that an integer has exactly two prime factors without revealing them. Their usefulness in this setting depends on whether the certificate preserves the difficulty of factoring. Motivated by the examples of Reble and Broadhurst, we formalize semiprimality certificates by adapting the Goldwasser-Kilian primality criterion. 2026/2619.title: Smaller Share Size for Evolving Secret Sharing: General Thresholds and Threshold Three
2026/2619.abstract: Evolving secret sharing allows participants to join indefinitely without modifying previously distributed shares. We study the share size of perfectly secure evolving threshold secret sharing schemes and obtain two results. For general thresholds, we introduce a polynomial sharing method that shares two secrets with adjacent reconstruction thresholds using one polynomial. Combining this method with the evolving scheme of Cheng et al.\ (ASIACRYPT 2025), we obtain an evolving $k$-threshold scheme whose $t$-th share has size \[ \left\lfloor \frac{k}{2} \right\rfloor \log_2 t + O_k\!\left(\ell+\lo

2026/2618.title: Efficient (Functional) Bootstrapping for CKKS over the Conjugate-Invariant Ring
2026/2618.abstract: The CKKS fully homomorphic encryption scheme enables efficient encrypted computation over complex-valued data. In many real-world cases, however, the computation only involves real data, and storing them inside complex slots wastes the encoding ability. This motivated the design of conjugate-invariant CKKS (CI-CKKS) instantiated over the conjugate-invariant ring (CIR), which provides the same number of real slots while halving the RLWE dimension. 2026/2617.title: Mutual Correlated Agreement and List-Decoding: Improvements and Separations
2026/2617.abstract: At a high level our contribution is threefold: we improve the quantitative MCA error bound for polynomial generators, we prove a refinement of the implication from list-decodability to MCA, and we clarify that in general, these two notions are distinct. We show that, for every finite field $\mathbb{F}$, every nonempty seed set $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}$, every linear code $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathbb{F}^{n}$ of relative minimum distance $\delta_{\mathcal{C}}$ and every degree $d \geq 1$, the univariate powers generator $G_{d}(x) := (1,x,\dots,x^{d})$ has mutual correlated agreement for $\mathcal

2026/2616.title: Descent-PBS: Programmable Bootstrapping beyond the Ring Dimension
2026/2616.abstract: Programmable bootstrapping (PBS) in FHEW/TFHE evaluates a lookup table (LUT) while refreshing a ciphertext, but a t-entry negacyclic table must fit, with redundancy, into the 2N signed rotation positions of a ring accumulator. Module bootstrappings, namely extended bootstrapping (PKC'23), monomial-matrix bootstrapping (TCC'25) and their successors, rotate a redundant table once in a module of rank tau, at a cost linear in both the rank and the redundancy.
