2026/2615.title: Faster and Smaller Anonymous Credentials from Standardized Signatures
2026/2615.abstract: We present GordieHowe, a system comprising a language, a certifying compiler, and a zero-knowledge proof protocol. GordieHowe is especially suitable for building anonymous credentials on top of standardized signature schemes like ECDSA, RSA, and ML-DSA. GordieHowe is the first system to achieve the following three properties simultaneously: provable security against quantum attackers, efficiency for statements spanning multiple fields—including proving and verifying in parallel—and automatic batching of structured computations. GordieHowe is high-assurance by design. The language is designed t

2026/2614.title: Tight Post-Quantum Multi-Key Security of the FX Construction
2026/2614.abstract: The FX construction (FX) is one of the simplest key-length extension schemes for block ciphers, introduced by Kilian and Rogaway as a generalization of DESX. By extending the key length without modifying the underlying block cipher, FX can improve security against adversaries that perform quantum computation but are restricted to classical queries to the keyed construction. Recently, Shiba and Iwata showed in their ToSC 2026 paper that FX with an $n$-bit block and a $\kappa$-bit internal key is secure up to approximately $2^{(n+\kappa-\log_2\mu)/3}$ total classical and quantum oracle queries i

2026/2613.title: Learning with Quantization and Worst Case Lattice Problems
2026/2613.abstract: Motivated by the MAMBA proposals, we study the worst case hardness of learning with quantization (LWQ) with public dither. We allow any efficiently computable dither function and efficiently samplable seed distribution; the matrix is uniform and independent of the secret and the seed. Using the randomized polar lattice quantizer of Lyu et al., we construct explicit families with polynomial power of two moduli. For the search family, polynomial time recovery of the uniformly chosen secret with inverse polynomial probability yields quantum polynomial time algorithms for the gap shortest vector p

2026/2612.title: Tritone: Pairwise Garbled Disputes for Multi-Party Proof Verification on Bitcoin
2026/2612.abstract: Bitcoin Script lacks native pairing operations for efficient direct verification of Groth16 proofs. Conventional federated bridges instead authorize withdrawals through a signing quorum, whose collusion can release funds without valid evidence. We present the Tritone protocol, which lets Bitcoin enforce the outcome of verifying a Groth16 proof for an NP relation fixed in a one-time trusted setup, with the locked funds secure as long as one of a fixed set of $N$ operators is honest. 2026/2611.title: For Thirty Pieces of Silver: Overcoming Non-IID via ZKP Sample-Level Auditing and Forcing Attackers into Traitors in Federated Learning
2026/2611.abstract: As a privacy-preserving distributed learning paradigm, federated learning faces severe security threats, especially data poisoning, gradient tampering, distributed attacks, and adaptive attacks. Existing gradient-based detection methods encounter three major bottlenecks in practical applications. First, they cannot distinguish between benign and malicious gradients under distributed attacks in non-IID scenarios. Second, defenders lack prior knowledge of trigger patterns. 2026/2610.title: A Crypto-Agile Mixed-Radix NTT Accelerator for Negacyclic and Trinomial Rings
2026/2610.abstract: Hardware accelerators for lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC) have largely converged on the radix-2 number-theoretic transform (NTT). The spectrum of standards that crypto-agility must accommodate, however, extends beyond NIST. In response to advances in cryptanalysis and to reduce the attack surface, national authorities are standardizing or recommending lattice-based algorithms with alternative algebraic structures, as well as schemes built on entirely different primitives. 2026/2609.title: SoK: Optimization Tools for the Hydra Multiplayer Channel
2026/2609.abstract: Blockchain technology allows parties to use a consensus protocol to add transactions and data to a decentralized ledger that are immutable. However, the amount of transactions that can be processed within a consensus protocol and thus added to the ledger within a given time frame is limited. This is a scalability issue. Layer-2 protocols are a class of approaches that process transactions off-chain, i.e. without involvement of the consensus protocol, but allow usage of the consensus protocol as a backup for security. 2026/2608.title: Pairwise Independence of Ten-Round AES
2026/2608.abstract: We prove that ten rounds of \AES{} with independent and uniform random round keys are $\varepsilon_{10}$-close to pairwise independent, with \[ \varepsilon_{10}\leq\frac{3017}{2^{141}}<2^{-129}. \] For every two distinct plaintexts, the joint ciphertext distribution is therefore within this statistical distance of the uniform distribution on ordered pairs of distinct ciphertexts. The same sampled key tuple is used for both encryptions. 2026/2607.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
2026/2607.abstract: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at TQC'21 and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (qOWFs). However, the question of the necessity of qOWFs for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public-keys and ciphertexts (qPKE) has remained open. 2026/2606.title: On the $s$-projected Goppa Codes and their Application to the Interactive Oracle Proofs of Proximity
2026/2606.abstract: Error-correcting codes are a useful tool in cryptography, being used both to design schemes whose hardness relies on coding theory problems (the area typically known as code-based cryptography) and as a building block in other contexts, such as proof systems and associated cryptographic argument systems. Among all codes used in cryptography, Goppa codes stand out, notably in the well-known McEliece encryption scheme, where they have withstood the test of time as one of very few classes of codes to be considered secure for over 40 years. 2026/2605.title: Mímir: A Stateless Private Search Engine
2026/2605.abstract: Private search engines allow a user to retrieve documents from a public database that are similar to a text query. Our cryptographic protocol Mímir employs state-of-the-art homomorphic ciphertext switching techniques to realize the first stateless semantic private search engine for highly dynamic databases. The security of Mímir relies on (Ring) Learning with Errors. Mímir requires no offline communication, and it trades higher but highly parallelizable server computation for low per-query communication. When the database may change between queries, Mímir matches Tiptoe's search quality with 8

2026/2604.title: Balsamic: One-round Threshold UOV from GPU-Accelerated FHE
2026/2604.abstract: Universal thresholdizers offer one-round threshold signatures, but require evaluating an entire signer under fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). We present Balsamic, a complete homomorphic Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) signer and its application to one-round threshold UOV signature. UOV's short salted target hash shifts the encrypted workload to finite-field linear solving, which we integrate with coin derivation and hashing in a packed discrete-CKKS circuit. 2026/2603.title: PPAD Hardness from SIS
2026/2603.abstract: Understanding the hardness of the complexity class PPAD is an important question in complexity theory given that it contains problems such as computing a Nash equilibrium. Evidence of hardness, however, has come primarily from cryptography, through a long line of work. Most recently, Chen, Freitag, Jin and Wichs (STOC 2025) based the hardness of PPAD on the polynomial hardness of the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem, together with a fine-grained average-case hardness assumption. 2026/2602.title: A Probabilistic Extension of the Division Property: Integral Distinguishers with Key-Independent Bounds
2026/2602.abstract: Classical integral cryptanalysis relies on zero-sum properties that, for every key, hold with probability one. Existing arguments against such deterministic integrals, based on the division property and its algebraic variants, only exclude this extreme case: once the zero-sum probability falls below one, they say nothing about its actual value, nor about a probabilistic bias that could still be exploited. 2026/2601.title: Integer Coordinate Families and Threshold RSA Signatures for Any Prime Exponent
2026/2601.abstract: At CT-RSA 2026, Ng and Lau introduced $(t,n)$-integer coordinate families for threshold RSA signatures with $e=3$, and found some families by heuristic search for $2\le t \le n \le 9$. They asked whether such families always exist and, if so, can they be constructed efficiently. We answer both of these questions positively. We prove that a $(t,n)$-integer coordinate family is also a $(t+1,n)$-integer coordinate family. 2026/2600.title: High-Precision Bootstrapping for GCKKS
2026/2600.abstract: Generalized CKKS (GCKKS) trades slot count for reduced modulus consumption in high-precision approximate arithmetic. However, designing a GCKKS bootstrapping algorithm with reduced modulus consumption throughout its computation remains a challenging problem. We construct high-precision bootstrapping for GCKKS using low-precision overflow extraction followed by iterative precision enhancement. Our main ingredient is a ciphertext-conversion framework for changing the decryption factor and slot count without requiring the factors to be units. 2026/2599.title: Linear Cryptanalysis of TFHE-Friendly Cipher FRAST in the Average Key Setting
2026/2599.abstract: In the average key setting, a linear attack of Bak et al. on the TFHE-friendly stream cipher FRAST let wrong guesses pass, which they left as an open problem. The S-boxes of FRAST are public and random for every keystream block. For the mask on the least significant bit, we show that key differences fall into five indistinguishable classes per round. The filter of Bak et al. gives some wrong classes of the right parity a nonzero expected score. 2026/2598.title: The Distributed Producer-Consumer Model Is All You Need: A Compiler for Asynchronous BFT
2026/2598.abstract: Building an Asynchronous Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) protocol requires establishing payload availability with total order despite Byzantine faults and arbitrarily delayed messages. Although many BFT systems separate payload dissemination from agreement, they often couple their composition to protocol-specific selection or scheduling mechanisms. We present the Distributed Producer-Consumer Model (DPCM), an event-driven abstraction that separates payload-specific certified availability from payload-oblivious binary finalization. 2026/2597.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Noisy: A Systematic Analysis of Ring-Oscillator-Based Noise Generators
2026/2597.abstract: Hiding countermeasures, alongside masking, play an important role in modern hardware security for protecting against side-channel attacks. Additive noise generators are one such hiding countermeasure. They increase the noise, thereby lowering the signal-to-noise ratio and, simultaneously, amplifying the effectiveness of masking countermeasures. Among the different design options for additive noise generators, ring-oscillator-based designs feature regularly in scientific publications. 2026/2596.title: ANNULAR: Post-Quantum Private Transactions from Isogenies with Recursive Batch Verification
2026/2596.abstract: ANNULAR is a shielded pool built on isogeny-based primitives. Notes are committed in a Merkle tree and spent by nullifier with hidden amounts, following the structure of Zcash's Sapling, but every primitive is post-quantum: spends are authorised by the prime-degree PRISM signature of Basso et al., note ciphertexts are keyed by the MIKE non-interactive key exchange, and each transaction carries a STARK proved natively over the isogeny field. 2026/2595.title: Getting to the right root: radical isogenies of every degree
2026/2595.abstract: Class group actions on supersingular elliptic curves over $\mathbb F_p$ as in CSIDH are typically evaluated as long chains of isogenies of small prime degree. Radical isogeny formulae compute such chains using a single $N$th root per step, without sampling torsion points. Compact formulae of linear size had been conjectured for all odd $N$. We prove a corrected version of these formulae for every $N\ge4$, odd and even, over every field of characteristic coprime to $2N$. 2026/2594.title: Registered Functional Encryption for Circuits with Dynamic Bounded Collusion
2026/2594.abstract: Registered Functional Encryption (Reg-FE) eliminates the key escrow issue in traditional functional encryption by allowing users to generate their own public/secret keys without the help of a central authority. The public key is then registered to the system along with a function, and all the registered public keys will be aggregated to a compact master public key by a transparent key curator. Messages are encrypted under the master public key, and users can learn functions of encrypted data from the ciphertext using their own secret keys. 2026/2593.title: Efficient Laconic Oblivious Transfer with Malicious Security
2026/2593.abstract: Laconic Oblivious Transfer (OT) enables a receiver to compress a large database into a short digest, allowing a sender to generate a succinct ciphertext that reveals only a single indexed message. While prior works achieve efficient constructions in the semi-honest model, known solutions for malicious security rely on inherently heavy non-black-box techniques, such as garbled circuits or succinct arguments, resulting in impractical schemes. 2026/2592.title: A Post Quantum Vector Commitment Scheme with Efficient Insertions and Deletions
2026/2592.abstract: Vector Commitments (VCs) are a cryptographic primitive that allows users to commit to a tuple and later provide proofs about entries of the committed tuple. Literature on VCs provides many secure constructions with properties attractive for decentralized applications. These include fast commitment/proof update algorithms after a value in the committed vector changes, algorithms to aggregate position proofs, generating proofs for subvectors, commitment hiding, and many more. 2026/2591.title: Sotto Maschera: Masking the Sota-Voce Fixed-Weight Vector Sampling
2026/2591.abstract: Sparse fixed-weight vector sampling is a highly critical primitive in several post-quantum cryptography schemes. It has also been the target of multiple side-channel attacks, demonstrating the need for robust implementations. While such implementations do exist, they are not necessarily practical in terms of runtime, and some have already been shown to be insecure. At CHES 2026, Filho et al. presented a runtime-optimized, but not side-channel protected, sparse fixed-weight vector sampling algorithm named Sota Voce. 2026/2590.title: Rerandomizable Garbling for Arithmetic Circuits
2026/2590.abstract: Rerandomizable garbling is a powerful extension of Yao’s garbled circuits that allows a garbled circuit to be refreshed without changing its functionality, while preserving privacy as long as at least one rerandomization step is honest. Existing constructions, however, are limited to Boolean circuits and incur significant communication overhead. In this work, we initiate the study of rerandomizable garbling for arithmetic circuits. 2026/2589.title: Cyclic isogeny walks on genus-zero modular curves
2026/2589.abstract: Isogeny-based cryptography implementations have to navigate a large space of options for representing elliptic curves and isogenies and for the corresponding arithmetic. This work collects, completes, and organizes the set of algebraic maps and relations available when working with genus-zero modular curves $X_0(N)$, which parametrize cyclic $N$-isogenies of elliptic curves and can be represented by a single field element. This abstract notion covers many single-parameter curve models, such as Montgomery, Edwards, Jacobi quartic, Hessian curve, Deuring normal form. Such single-parameter models

2026/2588.title: Eras MPC: Granular Preprocessing and Abort Recovery with Dynamic Committees
2026/2588.abstract: MPC with dynamic committees achieves scalability by having small committees execute each round of the computation, instead of involving all parties in the entire execution. However, achieving Guaranteed Output Delivery in efficient information theoretical protocols requires larger honest majority committees, limiting scalability. Moreover, using preprocessed correlated randomness to speed up the computation is prohibitively expensive due to the cost of transferring such randomness to parties that have not yet joined the execution. We propose Eras MPC, a model where small dishonest majority com

2026/2587.title: RingTrace: Model-Free Spatio-Temporal Detection and Core Attribution for Cache Side-Channels
2026/2587.abstract: The widespread adoption of shared last-level caches in modern multi-core processors improves memory efficiency but introduces timing channels between untrusted programs. In particular, Flush+Reload serves as a high-resolution cache side channel and a fundamental data leakage mechanism in transient-execution attacks. Existing detection approaches predominantly rely on aggregate hardware performance counters, which discard spatial context, fail to locate the malicious core, and often confuse stealthy attacks with benign cache-intensive workloads. This paper addresses these gaps by proposing Ring

2026/2586.title: Modeling Modular Multiplication for Monomial Prediction and Impossible Differentials, with Application to MSX
2026/2586.abstract: MSX is a recent family of lightweight block ciphers for microcontrollers, and its round function draws nonlinearity from modular addition and modular multiplication on $32$-bit words. The multiplication is the distinctive part of the design because it turns the round function into a strongly universal hash function, and from this, the designers prove ideal strong differential and linear properties. The same operation also kept MSX out of reach of automated cryptanalysis, since no exact bit-level model of a modular multiplication was available. We give two such models for $z=(x\cdot y)\bmod 2^n

2026/2585.title: Verifiable Post-Quantum TLS Handshake: Recognizing Implementation Errors of Cryptographic Verification Steps
2026/2585.abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is becoming unavoidable for security protocols. Yet as the historical "goto fail" incident illustrates, deploying new primitives is not sufficient: subtle implementation bugs, especially in verification logic, can yield systems that remain fully interoperable while compromising security silently. Existing confirmation code techniques make certain errors observable, but they do not cover post-quantum signatures and provide limited protection in multi-stage handshakes. Therefore, we present a migration-oriented solution that spans both the algorithm and

2026/2584.title: SHAKEing SLH-DSA with Non-profiled SCAs
2026/2584.abstract: SLH-DSA is a hash-based digital signature algorithm, standardised by NIST as a post-quantum signature scheme. While prior work has analysed the vulnerability of its pseudorandom function (PRF) to differential side-channel analysis (SCA), no prior work has thoroughly examined this vulnerability under SHAKE as the PRF, nor recovered a full secret seed in practice. In this work, we address this gap by first analysing the differential SCA vulnerability of SLH-DSA-SHAKE, examining the inputs to the PRF and the possible selection functions for an attack. Then, based on this analysis, we propose a me

2026/2583.title: Rounded Gaussians are Discrete Gaussians
2026/2583.abstract: Many lattice-based cryptographic schemes still require sampling integers following a Gaussian-like distribution. Depending on the application, this sampling should be generic to tackle variable (and possibly large) standard deviations and centers, with a low memory footprint, easily implementable in constant-time, and with the highest throughput. Combining all these features is very challenging, as shown by the numerous works on optimizing discrete Gaussian samplers. In contrast, the rounded Gaussian (and associated samplers), formalized by Hülsing, Lange and Smeets (PKC'18), seems to satisfy

2026/2582.title: SoK: Design-Level Backdoors in Block Ciphers Constructions, Detection, and Key Recovery
2026/2582.abstract: A block cipher is trusted once it resists every published attack and its S-boxes pass the standard tests. A design-level backdoor turns this trust against its users. Its designer hides a structure that only they can exploit, and that the usual tests miss. Four such backdoors have been published, by Rijmen and Preneel, Paterson, Bannier and Filiol, and Peyrin and Wang. Each paper shows what the hidden structure gives its designer. 2026/2581.title: Post-Quantum Sublinear Lookup Arguments from Polynomial Preprocessing
2026/2581.abstract: Lookup arguments with sublinear prover time typically rely on bilinear pairings. The only exception is the recent work of Campanelli, Carrillo, Cascudo, Fiore, Francati, and Gennaro (ePrint 2025/238); however, they rely on general-purpose SNARKs to certify expensive preprocessing, which requires non-black-box usage of cryptographic primitives. Thus practical realizations of sublinear lookups with post-quantum security remain challenging. 2026/2580.title: Table-Free Constant-Work BCH Decoding by Algebraic Index Elimination
2026/2580.abstract: Algebraic error-correcting codes such as BCH let lattice-based key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) reduce bandwidth and the decryption-failure rate. The decoder’s input is determined jointly by the long-term secret and a ciphertext that an adversary may choose. Variable work or table accesses that reveal error positions can enable key recovery even when the KEM uses implicit rejection. Walters and Sinha Roy (WSR) gave a constant-work BCH decoder whose fixed-address realization scans the entire field per protected lookup. We introduce algebraic index elimination, a table-free realization of WSR

2026/2579.title: Active and Passive Attacks against TPM 2.0-based Full Disk Encryption
2026/2579.abstract: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0-based full-disk encryption (FDE) has gained renewed importance with the rise of bring-your-own-device environments. Aside from Windows Bitlocker, which uses the TPM since the days of Windows Vista, FDE has also been recently adopted by several Linux distributions. We revisit tamper attacks against TPM 2.0-based FDE systems and analyze the security of current Windows and Linux implementations. We examine TPM 2.0 sealing mechanisms and demonstrate passive and active attacks against systems using discrete TPMs (dTPMs) connected via SPI, using a mini PC and a note

2026/2578.title: HAETAE on a Diet: Less Stack, Less Time on Low-End Microcontrollers
2026/2578.abstract: HAETAE has shorter public keys and signatures than ML-DSA, but the signing stack of its reference implementation reaches $158\, \mathrm{KiB}$ on Cortex-M4. The Low-Stack HAETAE implementation presented at CHES'26 brings the signing stack down to $5.7$-$5.9\,\mathrm{KiB}$; yet even HAETAE-2 still needs $8,718\,\mathrm{B}$ in a realistic IoT scenario, where the secret key and the signature buffer share the same SRAM. 2026/2577.title: Back to the Bits: Revisiting MAYO’s Data Representation for GPU and Tensor-Core Acceleration
2026/2577.abstract: MAYO, a multivariate quadratic signature scheme with small public keys and signatures, is a third-round candidate in the additional signature standardization process of the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Cloud and application servers receiving many independent signing requests need to batch them on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). MAYO's nibble-sliced representation suits CPU shuffle instructions or multiplication tables, but on GPUs it costs a memory access or several instructions per $\mathbb{F}_{16}$ multiplication. The existing GPU implementation cuMAYO (CHES 2026) uses t

2026/2576.title: Reverse Engineering IVXV: A Specification and Security Analysis of Estonia’s Internet Voting System
2026/2576.abstract: Estonia’s IVXV system is one of the world’s longest-running and largest-scale deployments of internet voting, yet it lacks a precise public specification of the protocol as implemented or security claims, which has left it difficult to audit independently. We address this as follows: First, we reverse engineer a detailed specification of IVXV as implemented—covering the setup, voting, tallying, and audit phases—comprising protocol-flow diagrams, pseudocode algorithms, and the core data structures, reconstructed from the public source code, official documentation, and configuration examples. 2026/2575.title: RDK-CKKS: A Framework for Rigorous Error Analysis of CKKS Computation
2026/2575.abstract: The CKKS scheme allows approximate arithmetic on encrypted data, and has found widespread use in privacy-preserving computation. A rigorous control of its homomorphic error is critical for both precision and security guarantees. In particular, in some settings such as IND-CPA^D or threshold settings, the latter computation error should be hidden at the time of decryption. This is achieved by noise flooding techniques, which require a precise upper bound on the computational error magnitude. 2026/2574.title: Broadcast and Trace from Lattices: Collusion-Resistant and Publicly Traceable
2026/2574.abstract: A broadcast and trace scheme combines broadcast encryption with accountability. Specifically, broadcast encryption is augmented with an algorithm for tracing traitors within a specified set, even if the given pirate decoder is created by an arbitrary collusion of users. As in broadcast encryption, the size of the ciphertext should be sublinear in the total number of users $N$. In this work, we generically construct collusion-resistant broadcast and trace that supports public tracing from attribute-based encryption with succinct ciphertexts and lockable obfuscation, both of which are known from

2026/2573.title: Hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings
2026/2573.abstract: We give a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm for finding hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ over any effectively presented finite chain ring $R$. We call auxiliary group elements or subgroups used to extract information through oracle queries \emph{probes}. For chain length at least two, elementary abelian socle probes first recover the complete flag modulo the maximal ideal. 2026/2572.title: DISCO*: DIstributed and SCalable Oblivious Joins and Oblivious Primitives
2026/2572.abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) let clients outsource computation to untrusted clouds, but they remain vulnerable to side-channel and leakage-abuse attacks. Recent work closes this gap by combining hardware enclaves with oblivious computation, which offers strong security guarantees yet struggles to meet the performance and scalability demands of real-world deployments. 2026/2571.title: A Spectral Theory of Local-to-Global Leakage
2026/2571.abstract: This paper studies how local leakages characterize the global leakage in additive secret sharing over a finite abelian group, which is a special case of linear secret sharing and side-channel masking. Our main finding is structural: local-to-global leakage is governed by two disjoint components---the magnitude of local leakage and its spectral alignment across shares, while existing literature attempted to characterize the global leakage only by local mutual information (MI). 2026/2570.title: Membership Inference in Privacy-Preserving Vector Search
2026/2570.abstract: Vector retrieval increasingly runs over sensitive embedding databases. Backend-compatible protections are desirable in such settings in that they transform the plaintext vectors while leaving the search algorithm itself unchanged. However, the protected database then leaks some geometry, that is, information about the distances between the stored vectors. We study membership-inference attacks on such leakage given a single database snapshot and known plaintexts. Our central finding is that membership privacy depends on how much geometry is revealed and on whether known plaintexts can be linked

2026/2569.title: Optimal Proofs of Sequential Work
2026/2569.abstract: In a proof of sequential work (PoSW), introduced by Mahmoody, Moran and Vadhan [MMV'13], a verifier can be convinced that a prover performed a computation of $T$ sequential steps. Such a proof is $(\delta, \lambda)$-sound if a malicious prover making at most $(1-\delta)T$ sequential steps can produce a valid proof only with probability $2^{-\lambda}$, even when using massive parallelism. Besides time-lock puzzles (TLPs) and verifiable delay functions (VDFs), PoSW are one of the central primitives in timed cryptography. 2026/2568.title: Efficient NTRU+ Implementations on Cortex-M
2026/2568.abstract: Post-quantum cryptography on embedded devices requires implementations that perform cryptographic operations efficiently within limited computation and memory. Most lattice-based KEMs use 2-way NTTs over power-of-two cyclotomic rings, and their embedded implementations have been studied extensively. In contrast, implementations of schemes based on 3-way NTTs, which combine radix-3 and radix-2 layers, remain scarce. This work therefore presents efficient implementations of NTRU+, a KEM built on 3-way NTTs, on Arm Cortex-M0+, M3, M4, and M7. We configure the layer fusion, modular arithmetic, and

2026/2567.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Fault Attacks and Countermeasures on ML-DSA Rejection Sampling
2026/2567.abstract: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of fault attacks on the rejection sampling of ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and of the countermeasures proposed against them. Using the identity \(\mathbf{Az} - ct = \mathbf{Ay} - c\cdot\mathbf{s}_2 = \mathbf{r}\), we prove that the quantity compared by the "third rejection test" of patent WO2025261784A1 is exactly \(\mathbf{r}_1\), which is already produced during signing, while check 2 passing is what implies \(\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{w}_1\). 2026/2566.title: Fault-Induced Nonce Repetition in Threshold Lattice Signatures: A Reveal-Structure Criterion, Cross-Scheme Analysis, and Detection Boundaries
2026/2566.abstract: Threshold ML-DSA is regarded as a deployment model that eliminates single-point key risk, and the NIST threshold call (IR 8214C) has likewise attracted many proposals. Existing security analyses, however, generally assume malicious or compromised protocol participants. For the threat of "physical faults in the devices of honest participants," single-party lattice signatures have been studied systematically for over a decade, whereas threshold schemes, to our knowledge, have not yet been systematically evaluated. 2026/2565.title: Further Elaborations on the Provable Dual Attack
2026/2565.abstract: The dual attack is one of the main strategies for attacking the learning-with-errors (LWE) problem. A recent line of work aims at provable analyses of dual attacks that rely on as few heuristic assumptions as possible. We present a provable dual attack that recovers a subvector $\boldsymbol{s}_{\mathrm{guess}}$ of the LWE secret, and we derive an explicit lower bound on its success probability without any heuristic assumption. 2026/2563.title: Regular Syndrome Decoding Is Easier Than Previously Estimated
2026/2563.abstract: The Regular Syndrome Decoding (RSD) problem is a structured variant of classical Syndrome Decoding and underlies a growing number of efficient cryptographic constructions, including zero-knowledge protocols, pseudorandom correlation generators, and MPC-in-the-Head signatures. Although RSD is generally believed to be computationally hard, recent works have shown that algebraic attacks can outperform information-set decoding on important RSD parameter regimes. Building on this line of work, we revisit the concrete hardness of RSD and show that many widely used parameter sets are substantially ea

2026/2562.title: A New Approach to Reducing Modulus Requirements in Homomorphic Computation: Precision Allocation in CKKS
2026/2562.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data subject to the prescribed security and precision requirements (allowable deviations from ideal results). Among all FHE schemes, CKKS is a representative scheme for approximate arithmetic, allowing the same operation on multiple values packed into a single RLWE ciphertext. Reducing ciphertext modulus \(Q\) for given output precision requirements under RLWE security constraints is a central challenge in homomorphic computation. However, despite advances in plaintext and ciphertext representations, algorithmic optimization

2026/2561.title: SALUS: Large-Scale Homomorphic Circuit Synthesis via Logic-Aware LUT Optimization
2026/2561.abstract: Recently, growing interests are developed in optimizing fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) circuits to enable Boolean function evaluations over ciphertexts. While existing works utilize functional bootstrapping (FBS) to efficiently evaluate logic gates, the evaluation efficiency for large-scale circuits remains limited. Recent advances introduce a fast ciphertext conversion method, making it feasible to evaluate look-up tables (LUTs) over homomorphic multiplexer operation. 2026/2560.title: Graphs and cycles in curve-based collision walks
2026/2560.abstract: In this work, we look at collision-based attacks both for elliptic curve and isogeny problems. Our main focus is on attacks in the multi-user setting, i.e., where one tries to recover all secret keys of a large set of $L$ public keys simultaneously, in a faster way than the total time required to attack each key individually. We consider three different problems: (1) the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves, (2) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$-curves, (3) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_p$-curves. 2026/2559.title: FN-DSA on Arm Cortex-M55: Revisiting a Floating-Point Lattice Signature with Native FP64 and Helium
2026/2559.abstract: FN-DSA has the shortest signatures among NIST's post-quantum signature standards, but on microcontrollers its signing is slow because the binary64 arithmetic it specifies is emulated with integer instructions. Previous speedups either change the arithmetic or the order of random sampling, so their signatures no longer match the known-answer tests (KATs) of the reference implementation, or rely on double-precision SIMD instructions that microcontrollers lack. 2026/2558.title: Registered ABE via Predicate Encodings, Revisited
2026/2558.abstract: Predicate encodings, proposed by Wee (TCC'14), are a simple framework that abstracts a variety of attribute-based encryption (ABE) schemes. Zhu et al. showed how to apply predicate encodings to registered ABE (Reg-ABE) using the same definition as in vanilla ABE (Asiacrypt'23). We provide a new definition of predicate encodings that is more suitable for registered ABE and allows us to obtain more efficient Reg-ABE schemes than those by Zhu et al. for predicates captured by predicate encodings. 2026/2557.title: Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures
2026/2557.abstract: With Q-day approaching, the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) has begun, with governments across the US, UK and EU mandating migration to quantum-resistant standards. This paper benchmarks the three NIST-standardised PQC algorithms—FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA)—across key generation, signing and verification operations, measuring both computational performance and energy consumption on a range of constrained IoT-class devices, from the 32-bit Raspberry Pi 1 and Zero to the 64-bit Raspberry Pi 4, as well as commodity laptop hardware. 2026/2556.title: Analysis of an AI based code distinguisher
2026/2556.abstract: Recently, DeepDistinguisher demonstrated the capability of transformer-like architectures to accurately distinguish Goppa codes from linear codes randomly generated, outperforming traditional distinguishers in certain settings. The purpose of our research is to examine the working mechanism of the mentioned machine learning algorithm. In particular, we explore the performance of the distinguisher using saliency maps and attention visualization techniques. We first identify a low-weight-row artifact present in the random instances used during training and show that the model partially relies on

2026/2555.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
2026/2555.abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension.

2026/2554.title: Concrete LDVR Attacks with Fewer Signers
2026/2554.abstract: We improve the concrete parameters of the attacks on the low-dimensional vector representation (LDVR) problem by Rodríguez García and Tessaro (ePrint 2026/2126), whose attack on canonical evaluation points uses $5{,}020$ signers. By combining their Chinese remainder theorem construction with a generalized birthday search over many challenges, we obtain a concrete attack with $488$ signers and $173$ corruptions over the Curve25519 scalar field. 2026/2553.title: Near-Optimal Early Stopping with Optimal Communication
2026/2553.abstract: Minimizing both the round and communication complexity of Byzantine agreement (BA) is a longstanding problem. In the synchronous setting, early stopping protocols aim to terminate in number of rounds that is proportional to the actual number $f\leq t$ of corruptions in an execution, rather than on the worst case threshold $t$. The lower bound on the round complexity for such protocols is known to be $\min\{f+2, t+1\}$ rounds. 2026/2552.title: CHARRM - Characterizing Hardware Leakage in the Robust Random Probing Model
2026/2552.abstract: Masking is a prevalent countermeasure against passive physical implementation attacks such as Side-Channel Analysis (SCA). Despite its theoretical soundness, the practical application of masking is often fraught with complexity and prone to errors, underscoring the necessity for automated security verification. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for efficient security verification in the $(g, t, c)$-robust $(p, \epsilon)$-random probing model. 2026/2551.title: Privacy with Leakage from Falsifiable Assumptions
2026/2551.abstract: An inherent challenge in cryptography is finding realistic and meaningful models and assumptions. Such assumptions must be fal- sifiable. For symmetric-key cryptography in the standard model (i.e., black-box without leakage), it is conjectured that we have identified the right assumptions: pseudorandom functions and permutations (PRFs and PRPs). However, when considering side-channel attacks (SCAs) that exploit physical side-channel leakage, the answer is less clear. 2026/2550.title: PPGA: A Framework for Privacy-Preserving Graph Algorithms using the Prepare/Propagate/Gather/Apply Paradigm
2026/2550.abstract: Privacy-preserving graph computation enables the secure analysis of graphs modeling social interactions and networks, financial transactions, etc., while keeping the graph private. One approach is to use secure multiparty computation (MPC), allowing different clients to contribute parts of a graph without need of disclosure, and multiple MPC protocols have been proposed for running message-passing-based graph analysis. 2026/2549.title: Firebolt: Fast, Lightweight, Malicious Non-Interactive Vector-OLE
2026/2549.abstract: We introduce a new maliciously-secure vector oblivious linear evaluation (VOLE), building upon a recent construction of (semi-honest) Paillier-based non-interactive VOLE. Our protocol is non-interactive (the sender can adaptively reveal entries of the VOLE using a single message to the receiver) and enjoys low communication (535 bytes for each VOLE entry) and low computation (around 5ms per party, single-threaded). 2026/2548.title: Evasive Inner Product Functional Encryption Is Broken Too
2026/2548.abstract: We show that the Evasive Inner Product Functional Encryption assumption introduced by Hsieh, Lin and Luo (Eurocrypt 2024) is false in its full generality. Our counterexample adds to a long sequence of works that have attacked different variants of Evasive LWE, taking down another instance that has been considered ``public coin'' (and hence safe) in the literature. 2026/2547.title: $\mathcal{iO}$ from LWE with Structured Preimage
2026/2547.abstract: Constructing $\mathcal{iO}$ from simple, safe assumptions in the post-quantum regime is an important problem with wide-ranging applications. In this work, we make progress towards this goal. We formulate a new, arguably simple assumption called LWE with Structured Preimage that suffices to build $\mathcal{iO}$. 2026/2546.title: New IND-CPA-D Attacks on BFV and BGV
2026/2546.abstract: IND-CPA-D security is an extension of IND-CPA security introduced in the context of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). It captures the situation where the computation result is known to the adversary; it is in particular necessary for FHE with threshold decryption. This work presents three new attacks in this situation on the BFV and BGV FHE schemes, when their parameters are instantiated with heuristic assumptions commonly used to enable correctness. 2026/2545.title: A Note on the Security of ECDSA with Presignatures or Biased Nonces
2026/2545.abstract: Over the years, several ECDSA security experiments have been proposed to enable faster distributed ECDSA signing. These experiments are not known to reduce to the standard ECDSA game, and recent work (Groth and Shoup, Eurocrypt 2022) shows that some are vulnerable, especially when combined with raw signing (signing hash digests directly, rather than pre-hashed messages) and additive key derivation. 2026/2544.title: Blind-DLPA: An End-to-End Framework for Profiled Blind Side-Channel Analysis
2026/2544.abstract: Conventional profiled side-channel analysis generally assumes that the plaintexts or ciphertexts associated with target traces are available during key recovery. We consider a profiled blind setting in which the attacker can obtain labeled traces from a profiling device using known inputs and keys, but observes only leakage traces from the target device. 2026/2543.title: A Key-Recovery Attack on the GTLN Knapsack Cryptosystem via Continued Fractions
2026/2543.abstract: We present a continued-fraction key-recovery attack on the knapsack-based public-key cryptosystem proposed by Gómez-Torrecillas, Lobillo, and Navarro (GTLN). The key observation is that ratios of public-key differences closely approximate rational numbers with small denominators, enabling their exact recovery by continued fractions. 2026/2542.title: From if to Oops: Turning a conditional into a key-recovery oracle
2026/2542.abstract: Deterministic variants of CSIDH remove randomness from the group action, either through implementation techniques or, as in Houben's deterministic CSIDH and OSIDH-LD, by design. Since earlier fault attacks on CSIDH mostly target random point sampling, determinism seems to close that avenue. We show that it opens another: every secret-dependent step occurs at a fixed, public point of every execution, so an attacker can fault the same step repeatedly. 2026/2541.abstract: We propose a deterministic lattice-reduction algorithm with bit complexity matching QR factorization up to logarithmic factors, and an implementation that uses fewer instructions than \texttt{flatter} (CRYPTO 2023) in our benchmarks. 2026/2540.title: Efficient and Compact High-order Masking Raccoon on Memory Constrained Devices
2026/2540.abstract: Raccoon, presented at CRYPTO 2024, is a provably secure lattice-based signature scheme featuring an $O(d \log{d})$ masking overhead. Although it did not advance beyond the first-round of NIST's additional call for post-quantum digital signatures, Raccoon remains a promising candidate due to its low masking overhead and strong provable side-channel resistance. 2026/2539.title: Implementing Predicate Encryption for Branching Programs: Private Computation over Key-Homomorphic Encodings Without FHE
2026/2539.abstract: Predicate encryption (PE) encrypts a message under an attribute that the ciphertext hides, allowing a secret key for a predicate to recover the message only when the attribute satisfies the predicate. Existing public-key implementations support useful specialized predicates, but enforcing heterogeneous conditions with one key requires an attribute representation fixed before encryption, which grows with the supported types of conditions and cannot express types it does not anticipate, such as regular expressions. Lattice-based PE for general circuits is far more expressive, but existing constr

2026/2538.title: Optimizing HQC with Enhanced Parallel Binary Polynomial Multiplication on GPUs
2026/2538.abstract: Graphics processing units (GPUs) are widely employed as accelerators in modern servers to handle key-establishment requests in bulk. Such deployments require the GPU implementation to sustain high throughput while keeping each request within its latency bound. In this work, we present a high-performance, end-to-end GPU implementation of Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC), a code-based key encapsulation mechanism (KEM). We propose two novel techniques to accelerate the dominant cost of HQC, which is binary polynomial multiplication over Galois Field GF(2). The first is a parallelization of the Frobeniu

2026/2537.title: SAT and Neural Network Filters for Misinjections in Fault Attacks
2026/2537.abstract: A misinjection, an injection that misses the fault form an attack assumes, can make an elimination fault attack discard the correct key. They occur when the attacker has not determined the timing of the device, and a random-delay countermeasure wider than the S-box layer can force them even on one who has. This paper presents a SAT filter that removes misinjections without the secret key, one injection at a time. It models the differential propagation from the injected round to the end of the cipher in SAT and rejects an injection when the model has no solution for the assumed fault and the ob

2026/2536.title: IISFA: Ineffective Instruction-Skip Fault Attacks on Bitslice Implementations
2026/2536.abstract: Redundancy countermeasures prevent differential fault analysis by withholding faulty ciphertexts. Ineffective fault analysis and statistical ineffective fault attacks exploit executions in which an injected fault leaves the result unchanged, using constraints on intermediate values or statistical bias to recover keys. In this paper, we present an Ineffective Instruction-Skip Fault Attack (IISFA) on bitsliced implementations protected by redundancy. A bitsliced instruction processes $m$ S-boxes simultaneously. Skipping it leaves the group unchanged exactly when all $m$ S-box inputs belong to it

2026/2535.title: Quantum State Search with Classical Interactive Advice
2026/2535.abstract: We study whether a quantum verifier can find a hidden quantum state by exchanging classical messages with an unbounded prover who knows the state. The verifier has access to a reflection oracle about the target. For a Haar-random $n$-qubit target, we prove that achieving constant average fidelity with the target requires $(q+1)^2(B+1)=\Omega(2^n)$, where $q$ is the number of verifier queries and $B$ is the total prover-to-verifier communication. The bound allows arbitrary classical interaction and unrestricted computation between queries. Our proof extends the lower bound of Aaronson and Kuper

2026/2534.title: Circular Dragon: $\widetilde{{O}}$ptimal Adaptively Secure Distributed Randomness/Key Generation and Parallel Broadcast
2026/2534.abstract: We present the first strongly adaptive common coin protocol, under the PKI setup (in the random oracle model and the algebraic group model, yet with no trusted dealer), that (i) achieves the optimal resilience $t< n/2$ in synchronous networks, and (ii) attains near-optimal asymptotics: near-quadratic communication $O(\kappa \lambda n^2\log n)$ and logarithmic rounds $O(\kappa\log n)$, with failure probability $\textsf{negl}(\lambda)+2^{-\kappa}$, where $\lambda$ (resp. $\kappa$) is the computational (resp. statistical) security parameter. Furthermore, the coin protocol assumes no memory erasur

2026/2533.title: Off-Key: Inconsistent MAC Keys Compromise Privacy in SPDZ-Family MPC
2026/2533.abstract: SPDZ-family protocols for maliciously secure multi-party computation protect secret-shared values with message authentication codes (MACs) under a secret-shared global key. Their security requires that all values and preprocessing used together be authenticated under the same key. We present Off-Key, a privacy attack that exploits violations of this requirement. Depending on which specific MAC check protocol is used, a corrupted party can either recover the value of a shared secret from a single authentication check or test a guess through selective failure by modifying a MAC share and observi

2026/2532.title: HERMES: High-Performance Private Decoding for Large Language Models
2026/2532.abstract: Privacy-preserving inference (PI) enables users to query large language models (LLMs) without revealing their prompts, but incurs substantial computation and communication overhead. Prior PI systems primarily optimize prefill and time to first token (TTFT). This suits applications that need only a single output token, yet most real-world use cases require multi-token responses. Such autoregressive workloads are dominated by time per output token (TPOT) instead. For the first time, we investigate generating full multi-token answers for real prompts under PI. We show that PI decode is hindered b

2026/2531.title: High-Precision CKKS with Focal Units
2026/2531.abstract: In CKKS, higher precision requires a larger scaling factor, increasing modulus consumption during homomorphic arithmetic and leaving less modulus available after bootstrapping under the same modulus budget. We introduce Focused CKKS, which trades unused SIMD slots for precision through focused rescaling and key-switching based on cyclotomic units. These units reduce error in selected focus slots while allowing larger error in the background slots. Using only a $1/k$ fraction of the slots provides approximately $k$ times as many bits of precision at the same scaling factor and CKKS parameter se

2026/2530.title: Computing endomorphisms of superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces in time and memory \(p^{4/5+o(1)}\)
2026/2530.abstract: We present an algorithm for computing endomorphisms of superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces over finite fields. Under a standard heuristic, we obtain a non-scalar polarized endomorphism in expected time and memory $p^{4/5 + o(1)}$.

2026/2529.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
2026/2529.abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $\rho(1,9)=242$. We first show that a function of nonlinearity $243$ would yield one of nonlinearity $244$, so it suffices to exclude $244

2026/2528.title: Revisiting the Security of VDOO
2026/2528.abstract: VDOO is a multivariate signature scheme submitted to the Next-generation Commercial Cryptographic Algorithms Program (NGCC). We study the security of its submitted parameter sets. In this paper, VDOO is described as a multilayer Rainbow construction. By retaining only its last oil space, we obtain a generalized UOV instance and apply existing wedge attacks. For the parameter set targeting 512-bit security, we estimate costs of $2^{432}$ and $2^{379}$ gates for the reconciliation and intersection variants, respectively. These estimates rely on the assumptions of the attack model and are below b

2026/2527.title: How Secure are NTRU+ Keys? Analysing the Best Module Attacks
2026/2527.abstract: A recent analysis of module-BKZ [Ducas–Engleberts–Perthuis, Asiacrypt'25] predicts subexponential speedups for lattice reduction on module lattices over cyclotomic fields whose conductor has small odd prime factors. This threatens NTRU+, the South Korean standard for key encapsulation, and related schemes; however, the short vectors one seeks to find are short in the coefficient geometry, whereas module-BKZ operates in the canonical geometry. We introduce relative canonical and relative coefficient embeddings, realising a module over a cyclotomic field $K$ as a module over any subfield $L$, an

2026/2526.title: Faster ABE for Turing Machines from Circular Evasive LWE
2026/2526.abstract: We present a new ABE for Turing machines, where - encryption runs in time $O(T)$ and produces a ciphertext of size $O(T)$ for time $T$ computation; - key generation produces a key of size $O(1)$; - security relies on the (public-coin) circular evasive LWE assumption. In fact, we obtain an ABE for a simple and more general model of computation which we refer to as iterated (local) computation. We improve on the recent construction of Agrawal, Kumari, and Yamada (CRYPTO 24) in three ways: (i) faster encryption and smaller ciphertext size; (ii) smaller key size, and (iii) weaker assumptions, elim

2026/2525.title: Enjoy FAEST on Hardware: Efficient and Novel Hardware Acceleration of Emerging Post-Quantum Digital Signature Scheme FAEST
2026/2525.abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) standardization process has drawn significant attention from the research community recently, especially regarding these PQC schemes' hardware acceleration. Nevertheless, related research on the emerging schemes, e.g., those currently under consideration by the NIST additional digital signature scheme standardization, still needs further exploration. With this background, this paper presents an efficient and novel hardware acceleration for FAEST, one of the promising signatures in the NIST Round 3 additio

2026/2524.title: Homomorphic Encryption for High-precision Arithmetic of Approximate Numbers
2026/2524.abstract: The CKKS fully homomorphic encryption scheme enables efficient arithmetic over complex numbers, but each homomorphic multiplication consumes a large modulus to ensure enough precision, limiting both the circuit depth and precision supported by CKKS. This work addresses this problem by proposing Generalized CKKS (GCKKS), a CKKS analogue of the GBFV scheme (EUROCRYPT 2025) that trades the number of slots for reduced modulus consumption. Despite its high-level similarity to GBFV, GCKKS faces new challenges caused by the different encoding and encryption structures of CKKS. We address these challe

2026/2523.title: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Security Analysis
2026/2523.abstract: All traditional encryption schemes share a fundamental operational vulnerability: encrypted data must be decrypted before it can be used. Fully homomorphic encryption eliminates this vulnerability by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, but existing FHE schemes impose substantial practical constraints that limit deployment. This paper presents a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key FHE scheme. GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

2026/2522.title: Superspecial points on Humbert surfaces and the probability of (N,N)-splitting
2026/2522.abstract: Let $p\equiv3\pmod4$ be a prime and let $N\geq2$ be an integer. We determine, to first order in $1/p$ and with an explicit error bound, the proportion of superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ that are optimally $(N,N)$-split. The surfaces are weighted by the reciprocals of their automorphism orders, which is the stationary measure of the Richelot random walk. The main theorem states that for $p\nmid N$ the expected number of optimal $(N,N)$-splittings of a surface is exactly $5NJ_2(N)(p-1)/(p^2+1)$, where $J_2$ is Jordan's totient; that for $p>2N^2$

2026/2521.title: Eﬃcient Fixed-Point Implementation of Mitaka
2026/2521.abstract: The Mitaka signature scheme is a variant of Falcon (FN-DSA). It has a considerably simpler signing procedure that can be parallelized while retaining Falcon's efficiency advantage. Mitaka offers two different signing approaches: a default one relying on floating-point arithmetic and an alternative, called MitakaZ, avoiding floating-point arithmetic at the cost of more Gaussian samples. Despite its better portability, MitakaZ has not previously been implemented in practice. This work presents an efficient fixed-point implementation of the Mitaka signing algorithm. We optimize the MitakaZ Gaussi

2026/2520.title: GPU Acceleration for Boyar-Peralta Algorithm in High Dimensional Linear Layers
2026/2520.abstract: The design of lightweight cryptographic schemes necessitates efficient circuit implementations of linear layers. A commonly used metric for evaluating circuit efficiency is the number of XOR gates required. For a given linear transformation over $\mathbb F_2$, finding its circuit implementation with the minimum number of XOR gates is referred to as the Shortest Linear Program (SLP) problem. As a prominent heuristic, the Boyar-Peralta (BP) algorithm provides competitive results, and numerous subsequent studies have introduced further optimizations. However, the inefficient implementations of th

2026/2519.title: DPA-style Attacks on VOLE-in-the-Head Signature Schemes
2026/2519.abstract: VOLE-in-the-Head (VOLEitH) has emerged as a promising paradigm for the design of post-quantum signatures, as it enables efficient signing and verification while also achieving small signature sizes. In the ongoing NIST PQC standardization process for additional digital signatures, two VOLEitH signature schemes, namely FAEST and SDitH, have advanced to the third round. Regarding their practical security, especially resistance to power side-channel attacks, existing studies have focused on only a few specific operations, and thus a comprehensive analysis remains lacking. To address this gap, we

2026/2518.title: Associated-Data Correlations in Eevee: Deterministic Forgeries against Nonce-Misuse Security
2026/2518.abstract: Eevee's Umbreon and Espeon modes claim online authenticated-encryption security under nonce reuse. We give an independent analysis of associated-data correlations that yield probability-one non-empty-message forgeries with three encryption queries and one verification query. Two AD-only tags reveal a mask difference that translates a ciphertext to another AD value. The basic attacks and their proof diagnosis overlap with independent and concurrent work by Mao et al. Our complementary contribution is a systematic affine treatment of partial final message blocks. For any admissible fixed final-f

2026/2517.title: Zippel: A Language, Compiler, Runtime, and Analyzer for ZK Proof Systems
2026/2517.abstract: This paper introduces Zippel, a language, compiler, runtime, and analyzer for cryptographic proof systems. Zippel lets developers write proof systems with ease using syntax that mimics pseudocode in cryptography papers. It also eliminates entire classes of vulnerabilities by construction owing to its type system and runtime. For example, Zippel automatically synchronizes protocol transcripts and correctly applies the Fiat--Shamir transform. Zippel also has fully automated static analyses that confirm whether a protocol is complete and sound given only the protocol's description. We have implem

2026/2516.title: Watermarking Proofs with Provenance-Binding ZK-SNARKs
2026/2516.abstract: The emerging ecosystem of outsourced proving services, decentralized prover networks, and prover marketplaces raises a new requirement for ZK-SNARKs: the need to watermark proofs with provenance information, such as the prover identity and a fresh request-time nonce. The prover identity records who should receive credit for the proof, while the nonce binds the proof to a particular request and is intended to prevent the prover from reusing work performed before that request was created. The key security requirement is that a prover must perform fresh work—comparable to computing the proof from

2026/2515.title: CHAMP: Cayley HAshing with Matrix Products
2026/2515.abstract: Cayley hash functions hash binary strings by representing the bits of the message as elements of a semigroup and multiplying the corresponding elements. This gives Cayley hash functions useful homomorphic properties. Here, we propose CHAMP, a Cayley hash function based on products of $2\times 2$ matrices over a finite field, and discuss its security, implementation, and performance.

2026/2514.title: Analysis of the Multi-Key Optimization for SPECK
2026/2514.abstract: SPECK has recently been introduced as a code-based digital signature scheme exploiting the similarities between the Permuted Kernel Problem (PKP) and the Permutation Code Equivalence Problem (PEP). By utilizing PEP as a trapdoor for PKP, SPECK achieves a significant speedup compared to LESS, replacing expensive Gaussian elimination with vector-matrix multiplications. This comes at the cost of larger signatures, since each round of the Zero Knowledge (ZK) protocol used in SPECK has soundness error $1/2$. A well known technique to reduce the soundness errors (and thus the number of parallel repe

2026/2513.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption for Small Batches of Complex Numbers
2026/2513.abstract: We propose a new approximate homomorphic encryption scheme to process small batches of complex numbers. Leveled operations are based on a new shaped rounding, whose error is a multiple of a fixed public ring element $g$, small on the data slots and larger on the others. The unused slots form a guard band that is computed on but never decoded, and the polynomial scaling factor $g^{-1}\Delta$ generalizes the CKKS scaling factor, with $g=1$ recovering CKKS. Guard-domain bounds determine the scaling factor needed for stability, while a norm bound limits the precision gain for a given guard amplifi

2026/2512.title: SLEEK: Sparse Quasi-Cyclic Codes with Closed-Form DFR Key Encapsulation
2026/2512.abstract: Performance in terms of bandwidth and execution time, as well as decoding failures remain important challenges for code-based KEMs. This paper introduces SLEEK: Sparse quasi-cycLic codEs with closEd-form DFR Key encapsulation, a Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) based on Quasi-Cyclic Moderate-Density Parity-Check (QC-MDPC) codes. The scheme employs a parallel bit-flipping decoder with three iterations and a closed-form estimate of the decoding-failure rate (DFR). The latter allows parameter selection with analytically bounded failure probability and supports the use of standard IND-CCA transfo

2026/2511.title: I Want to Ride My BIKE: Customizing Bit-Flipping Decoders for Ephemeral Key KEMs
2026/2511.abstract: Large public keys and ciphertexts remain a major obstacle to the deployment of post-quantum cryptosystems in applications currently relying on compact classical schemes. In code-based post-quantum key encapsulation mechanisms, reducing the Decoding Failure Rate (DFR) generally requires larger parameters, further increasing communication and storage overheads. Ephemeral key-pair scenarios allow a different trade-off: ideally, each secret key is used for a single decapsulation, limiting the opportunities to observe and exploit decryption failures. We investigate how this setting can be used to r

2026/2510.title: Secure Compilation of Probabilistic Side-Channel Countermeasures
2026/2510.abstract: Probabilistic countermeasures are a common means of protecting programs against side-channels. These countermeasures are hard to implement and are routinely broken by compilers. Proving that a compiler preserves probabilistic side-channel security directly would require reasoning about perfect simulatability of distributions, a challenging technique normally reserved for high-assurance cryptography in frameworks like EasyCrypt and out of scope for compiler correctness. In this paper, we present a language- and leakage-model-agnostic framework for provably secure compilation of probabilistic si

2026/2509.title: Sparse Secrets, Dense Problems: Efficiently Masking HQC in Hardware
2026/2509.abstract: HQC has recently been selected by NIST as a code-based alternative to ML-KEM and is currently undergoing standardization. While multiple timing and power side-channel attacks against HQC have been presented, application of masking has so far only been studied for software implementations. As part of this work, we close this gap by first proposing a novel masking technique for the sparse-dense vector multiplication, one of the core components in all HQC operations. We manage to securely exploit the sparsity of the secret operand using a mixed Boolean and arithmetic masking technique and prove i

2026/2508.title: Power Analysis on SQIsign via Ideal Reconstruction from Quaternion Leakages
2026/2508.abstract: SQIsign is an isogeny-based signature scheme, which is one of the Round-3 candidates for NIST's additional post-quantum digital signature standardization. NIST considers resistance to side-channel attacks as one important factor in evaluating digital signature schemes. However, side-channel analysis of SQIsign remains very limited. To the best of our knowledge, all existing studies target the Round-1 version, so their applicability to the substantially revised Round-3 SQIsign has not been established. Moreover, existing studies either provide experimental validation only for toy parameters or

2026/2507.title: safeRNSgcd: Accelerating Falcon key generation with RNS in SafeGCD
2026/2507.abstract: The deepest level of Falcon's NTRU solver needs only one Bézout coefficient from two large integer resultants already represented in a residue number system (RNS). We give $\mathtt{safeRNSgcd}$, which computes this coefficient while keeping the large states in RNS. Its central insight is that centered explicit CRT can recover the exact low bits needed by SafeGCD batches using single-word fixed-point arithmetic. Integrated into $\mathtt{ntrugen}$, our C implementation reduces inversion and private-key basis-generation costs on a Raspberry Pi 5 and two x86-64 processors, compared with original $

2026/2506.title: Efficient Two-Dimensional Representation Evaluation via Dual Isogenies with Applications to Isogeny-Based Cryptography
2026/2506.abstract: The evaluation of two-dimensional isogeny representations is a fundamental operation in many isogeny-based cryptographic schemes, notably the public-key encryption schemes POK\'{E} (Eurocrypt 2025) and PIKE (PKC 2026), as well as the digital signature schemes SQIsign2D-West (Asiacrypt 2024) and SQIsign2DPush (Eurocrypt 2026). However, existing two-dimensional evaluation algorithms rely on time-consuming discrete logarithm computations and torsion-basis generation, creating a severe performance bottleneck for the entire protocol. In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm for evaluating two-di

2026/2505.title: AVX-512 Acceleration of SQIsign 3.0 Verification
2026/2505.abstract: SQIsign is a compact isogeny-based signature scheme. We present a low-latency AVX-512 implementation of complete SQIsign 3.0 verification at security levels I, III, and V. Our implementation provides vectorized curve-side verification, including the Superglue transition, and introduces dynamic-programming strategies for the degree-$2^\ell$ and theta-model $(2,2)$-isogeny chains. The strategies account for batched point evaluation and the preparation of SIMD data. On an Intel Core i7-11800H running native Ubuntu 24.04, the complete verifiers achieve $2.14\times$, $2.08\times$, and $2.34\times$

2026/2504.title: Byzantine Broadcast in $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ Communication
2026/2504.abstract: We present a deterministic $n$-party Byzantine broadcast protocol secure against $t<n$ faults, with communication complexity $O(n^2\log^4(n)\lambda)$ and $O(t)$ rounds (where $\lambda$ is a security parameter), improving upon the seminal Dolev--Strong protocol from 1983.

2026/2503.title: SwiftAuth: Conditional Privacy-Preserving UAV Authentication with Multi-Source Credential Aggregation and Non-Interactive Authorization
2026/2503.abstract: To address the challenges of interactive credential issuance and conditional privacy-preserving authentication for dynamic terminals accessing multiple third-party services, we propose an traceable and aggregatable tagged witness signature (TA-TWS). Building upon this scheme, we design an efficient and privacy-preserving anonymous authentication framework, termed SwiftAuth. SwiftAuth decouples the issuer’s authorization phase from the user’s credential acquisition process in traditional anonymous authentication systems by introducing an asynchronous credential distribution mechanism. This allo

2026/2502.title: Shorter Hash-Based Signatures via Guarded Sharing in a DAG Model
2026/2502.abstract: Stateless hash-based signatures are among the most important post-quantum signature schemes. Although they have been standardized by NIST, they still have large signatures. Within these constructions, the few-time signature component is receiving increasing attention. Recent work has introduced new techniques, including rejection sampling, forced pruning, bucket thinning, and hash chains. In this work, we continue to improve few-time signatures with a new technique, guarded sharing. Our construction moves beyond the previous tree-based model to a DAG-based signature. By combining guarded shari

2026/2501.title: Aerie: Efficient Aggregation of Falcon Signatures
2026/2501.abstract: The post-quantum signatures selected by NIST are ten to over a hundred times larger than the elliptic-curve signatures they replace. Moreover, unlike the BLS signatures that blockchains use to aggregate validator votes, they do not aggregate natively. Both problems can be addressed with a SNARK: a short proof that a batch of signatures is valid, replacing the signatures themselves. The prevailing approach, central to Ethereum's roadmap, pairs hash-based signatures with hash-based SNARKs. This is slow because the prover must prove many hash evaluations per signature. We instead aggregate lattic

2026/2500.title: Threshold Post-Quantum E-Voting from Lattice Commitments
2026/2500.abstract: Lattice-based homomorphic e-voting protocols built on commitments, such as EVOLVE, keep ballots private against all but one authority and the tally verifiable even if all authorities collude, but need every authority to tally. We present T-EVOLVE, in which votes are Shamir-shared over the commitment message space: any t of n authorities that took part in the checking phase complete the tally, privacy holds against t-1 colluding authorities and verifiability against all. The voter proves that her committed shares form a Reed-Solomon codeword whose value at zero is a valid vote; the parity check

2026/2499.title: GhostFaceMPC: Privacy-Preserving Face Recognition with Multi-Party Computation
2026/2499.abstract: Facial recognition has become central to modern authentication systems, security frameworks, and personalized services. However, its widespread adoption is hindered by severe privacy risks, particularly surrounding unauthorized access to sensitive biometric data. To address these challenges, this paper presents GhostFaceMPC, the first end-to-end, privacy-preserving face recognition system to evaluate a deep convolutional neural network extractor and matching under secure multi-party computation. GhostFaceMPC enables secure processing of facial data across all stages of a face recognition proce

2026/2498.title: Noise-Tolerant Quantum One-Time Programs Using Stateless Trusted Hardware, Revisited
2026/2498.abstract: A quantum one-time program scheme is a functionality-preserving compiler that transforms a program into a quantum state that can be used to obtain only one output of the program. Our goal is to design quantum one-time programs that can be realized on existing quantum technologies. Our contributions are two-fold: 1. We design a BB84 state-based quantum one-time program scheme in the stateless trusted hardware model that is resilient to single-qubit corruption errors and detectable erasure errors. To illustrate, under independent noise with a 90% detectable erasure rate and a 3% Pauli Y-error ra

2026/2497.title: SecAgg++: A Post-Quantum Privacy Preserving Federated Learning Protocol
2026/2497.abstract: Secure aggregation is a fundamental building block for privacy-preserving federated learning, yet most existing masking-based secure aggregation protocols do not provide post-quantum security. In this work, we present SecAgg++, a masking-based post-quantum secure aggregation protocol for the single-server setting. SecAgg++ integrates post-quantum cryptographic primitives while preserving the communication and computational efficiency of classical frameworks such as SecAgg and SecAgg+, and supports client dropout handling through an efficient recovery procedure.

2026/2496.title: Structural Cryptanalysis of the Eevee AEAD Family
2026/2496.abstract: Eevee is a family of three AEAD modes, Umbreon, Jolteon, and Espeon, proposed at CCS 2023 for IoT-to-cloud secure computation. We analyze structural flaws in the algorithms of the supplied full-version specification and the proof steps underlying their online authenticated-encryption claims. An AD-free, two-encryption prefix distinguisher has advantage $1-2^{-n}$ in the ideal-forkcipher model, contradicting the specified online ideal object. 2026/2495.title: Issuer-Independent Decentralized Exchange for E-Cash
2026/2495.abstract: Despite decades of cryptographic advances, electronic cash (e-cash) remains largely confined to payments and lacks the broader decentralized financial applications built around cryptocurrencies. As a step toward broadening its application layer, we present an issuer-independent e-cash exchange in which a liquidity provider holds inventories of two independently issued e-cash currencies and users trade between them without requiring either issuer to participate in individual swaps. Our design combines a blockchain settlement layer, which automates the exchange and makes its execution publicly v

2026/2494.title: Speeding up Sumcheck using Algebraic Geometry
2026/2494.abstract: The sumcheck protocol, a ubiquitous component of modern proof-systems, enables proving the sum of evaluations of a low-degree multivariate polynomial. In theory, sumcheck has been generalized from polynomials to (tensors of) any multiplication code, a code whose pointwise products of codewords lie in a related product code. All practical systems nonetheless specifically use polynomials. For proof-systems over binary fields that target Boolean circuits, this choice has a real cost: the product of two binary messages under Reed--Solomon is no longer binary. As a result, the prover's work in the

2026/2493.title: Robust ECDSA Threshold Signing at Scale
2026/2493.abstract: This work presents an efficient, scalable, and robust threshold ECDSA signing protocol for the $t\leq (n-1)/3$ scenario, making it suitable for e.g., bridging consensus from one Blockchain to another. Our construction allows to batch-compute pre-processing material for efficient online signing. While our protocol is based on established ideas for (Verifiable) Secret Sharing, we optimize it to scale efficiently both in terms of computation and communication with a large number of signers. We therefore combine efficient batching techniques for sharing (Fitzi & Hirt, PODC 2006), randomness extrac

2026/2492.title: Exploring Fault Injection Attacks on HQC and BIKE Beyond Fujisaki-Okamoto Verification
2026/2492.abstract: Fault injection attacks have been extensively studied in the context of post-quantum cryptography, yet existing analyses on code-based KEMs largely focus on faults targeting the Fujisaki-Okamoto transform. This work presents new fault injection attacks against BIKE and HQC that operate beyond this commonly protected component and target less obvious instructions within the decapsulation process. The proposed attacks achieve full key recovery using only valid ciphertexts under NIST Level 1 parameters, requiring 17392 and approximately 3 million decapsulation queries for HQC and BIKE, respective

2026/2491.title: Shift-Invariant Permutations with Polynomial Composition: Construction and Algebraic Structure
2026/2491.abstract: Shift-invariant permutations of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) are particularly attractive in symmetric cryptography because of their regularity and implementation efficiency. Constructing such permutations with an explicit algebraic structure remains a challenging problem. In this paper, we study a family of shift-invariant transformations of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) constructed from a recursively defined sequence of mappings \(\{\gamma_j\}_{j\ge 0}\) associated with landscapes. First, we prove that, under an explicit dimension condition relating \(n\) to the support of the landscape, the sequence \(\{\gamma_j\}

2026/2490.title: Reaction Attack on CKKS Deployments with Asymptotically Optimal Query Complexity
2026/2490.abstract: We study a protocol-level reaction leakage in CKKS deployments where public coefficient-to-slot (C2S) evaluation keys are combined with a client's 1-bit validity response. Under this deployment surface, a malicious evaluator can recover a ternary secret key using asymptotically optimal $O(\mathcal{H})$ reaction queries, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the entropy of the secret key. The attack does not break RLWE or CKKS IND-CPA security. Instead, it exploits the interaction between client-side validity reactions and public homomorphic linear transformations.
